title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference 9.20.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Mike, just your reaction to this.  Just Yes. Uh, something weird.  Difficult, um, obviously to process, the second half was very different from the first. I think, you know, I think we brought it on ourselves.  I mean, we had 12 plays basically until the last two runs, and I don't remember a moment like that, so credit to them.  They're a really good team, um, obviously in all phases.  In the first half, you know, we didn't get the points, obviously.  We were tied 7-7 at halftime. But I mean, I felt like we had good control of the game and all phases, and I think we were like two out of eight on third chances in the first half, but always in manageable situations, and we just did some uncharacteristic things.    It's about small details, like I told the guys, when you play against really good teams, you don't have to do anything extraordinary, but do the ordinary in an extraordinary way, and we certainly didn't do that, especially on offense. You had 150 total yards or 100. Beyond the obvious, but yes. And on offense, you say?  Yes, I mean , that's exactly what I just said; We had some opportunities, especially in the first half, where I thought we could have scored and that we had good control.    I'm referring to possession time and all that kind of stuff.  And then, in the second half, there was no fluidity.  I mean, three and out, six and out, three and out, and when that happens, you're not going to get yards. So I couldn't point to just one thing, but it felt like that sequence where they forced the fumble and still gained 35 extra yards, then a penalty and ended up scoring;  There was a drastic change in the game. Yes, you could easily say that. I know that will be part of the narrative , but hey, they did it.  It's like, hey, you know what?  Hats off to them , great, you know, um, they ended up hitting, you know, what we call zero coverage, and I thought Drew made an amazing play to get the touchdown right there. Uh, but we had a chance, we were down by seven and uh, you know, then we ended up going down with three plays and out.  I thought it was something like in the next series when they went 10 up.  Um, you know, where things really started to change for us, and then again , we went six and out.  Um, again, it's not like a radical change is needed by any means.  We're not pressing any panic buttons, but when you're playing against the best defense, you have to do all the little things right, you know, and uh, we did n't do that today.  Um, but again, I like it, whenever there's an execution problem, for me that starts with training.  So we need to give them more clarity and then put them in better positions to succeed. It seemed that the aerial game couldn't really accomplish anything when Jacoby was under pressure.  What influenced that from your perspective? Yes I know.  I think you're right.    I mean , it's whether they're bringing the pressure or bringing four men. Mike is as good as anyone in the world, you know, switching, sending four, overloading you, stuff like that.    You're never going to have control of them because, I mean, he basically has a repertoire and he does a great job with it, obviously.  Um, but uh , you know, if it was a four-man press and just gaining a bit of an advantage or something.  So, um, you know, we need to look at the tape and obviously improve after all this. That last Seahawks series lasted more than 10 minutes, 16 plays, 15 carries.  How much does that destroy the will of your defense and your team? Yeah, I mean, obviously it was probably a long shot, you know, to be down by 17 at that point.  If it's a 16-point game, then you feel a little differently about, hey, getting a quick stoppage.  Um, our boys were fighting out there.  I'm not going to question that they were fighting. They fought in that last series to reach fourth and inches.  I told them I appreciate that, you know.  They did not back down .  Uh, it took everything Seattle had at that time, because I've also been on the other side, where, you know, you want to score a touchdown on offense and our guys made it hard.  But, uh, again, you know, credit to them, but a lot to correct on our end. Marvelous, Marvelous. Yes, exactly what I just said.  I mean, you know, you get to halftime and, again, we didn't have the points on offense, but there were, there were some good things.  I thought we were doing decent things on first and second down against a really good defense, but when you're on those manageable third downs, you have to move the chains and take advantage of the momentum those conversions give you, and we did n't.  But I thought our defense played excellently, obviously, you know, they score on the second play of the game, okay, great.  Um, on our second play we had an opportunity and we were a little disconnected in terms of our execution, and they got a great touchdown, when we thought we should have gotten it on that second play, and instead, it didn't happen .  We had to throw it on the ground right there .  So, um, a lot to correct.  I'm excited to be working with these guys again tomorrow. Marvelous caught two passes and was only on the field for about two-thirds of the time.  What was the reason for that?    I mean , I wouldn't overthink it ;  Obviously Trey had some, but I wouldn't attach much importance to anything right now, because we threw the fatal ball anyway .  So, again, schematically it wasn't good, you know. Was being out for so many plays a technical decision made before the game?  I... I think part of that was, obviously, using heavyweight personnel, so you end up having only one receiver on the field.  We were on what we call 13 Z, and that's where Mike is our catcher.  When we're on 13 X, which we had a couple of plays like that, Marv is our receiver.  That's all. Are you worried about their current situation? Uh, not worried, no.  You know, I'm concerned about our offensive execution today, but I think it's all something we know we can do better. We know we can train him better and we have a higher standard than that. What is your perspective on what went wrong with the coverage of JSN throughout the day? In the game. Yeah, I mean, it's a really good receiver, you know?  I mean, that second play of the game is one you obviously want to recover because it really doesn't matter who it is.  It's, you know, we're better than that. From an execution point of view only, obviously, but he's a really good receiver.  I mean, it's possibly the best, and like I always say, I know you're not going to love it, but I have to watch the tape with the defense.  You know, I see the effort.  I see all that kind of stuff.  You guys see the flashy plays, so to speak, but I 'm more focused on, obviously, organizing our series and all that kind of stuff.  I need to make sure there's a smooth flow to what's happening on defense, but I need to review the tape a little more about that. What does your instinct tell you about the balance between plan and execution today? Uh, it just wasn't good enough overall.  You know, the scheme clearly wasn't good enough.  Every time you have about 120 yards before that final series.  I mean, that's not good at all.  So we knew it was going to be difficult.  Again, me , you know, if I want to be optimistic. I thought there were some things in the first half that we were doing quite well.  I thought, you know, we were getting some yards against a good defensive line.  Um, you know, but again, you don't have to be extraordinary, but you do have to do the ordinary things that we rely on very well, and we didn't. With JSN, what was the game plan coming in? Did it focus on him in the passing game? Yes, I mean, you know, you don't want to , um, let me say this the right way.  Uh, you don't want to sacrifice stopping the race and stuff too just for that, you know?  Um, so you're, you're mixing and matching.  Um, but uh, um, I'm not necessarily worried, I don't even know what that is, so I'm not concerned schematically in terms of what he was doing.  He'll have his moments.  We need to limit it and help our boys, but, you know, I don't think that was the case.  I thought we were playing really good defense, really until probably those, you know, last 20 minutes and, um, you know, um, they just took control from there on. Yes, it's a good team.  I mean, that's like the gold standard right now .  And it doesn't get any easier next week.  This team we're going to play against next week, you know, is going to be really good, and they're on a roll right now and they're healthy, and you see how good that team can be when they're healthy.  What cannot happen is that we cannot let Seattle beat us twice.  Not necessarily the second time we play against them.    I don't mind .  I don't even know when we play them again, but we can't let this affect next week and I don't think it will.    I love the guys in that locker room. We have great leadership.  And again, you know, I think an hour and a half, two hours ago, you guys were probably sitting there at halftime thinking, well, we've got a good game here.  And then, but it's 60 minutes.  And against a great team , you have to play 60 minutes against them.  And again, we didn't do it, and it starts with us as coaches. Melvin and Will Johnson both left the game.  What about them? Max has a... I'll have more information for you tomorrow.  Max has one foot and Will has the neck.  So. Is it serious initially?    I do n't believe it.  Um, I don't think so.  Uh, but we'll find out a little more tomorrow.  So, both of them, they both said , you know, they looked me in the eye and said, "I'm fine," but you know, sometimes the adrenaline rushes and then you wake up the next morning and, um , you know, they're watching the coaches right now while the adrenaline is coming down and sometimes you feel some kind of discomfort.

I mean, you've got to win your one-on-one matchups. We're built for our explosive interior players uh to be able to win those matchups, and we won more of them than we did the week before. And that that's going to continue uh because I know our guys will continue to work and they'll continue to uh to improve. >> Thanks, we'll go to Ashley. >> Hey, Todd. Um, I just first wanted to ask about the decision to challenge when you did and the the challenge that you guys lost. Just what was the thought process there with that? >> Well, the between third and four and third and eight to me is is pretty big. And between upstairs and myself, we didn't think he got the third foot down on the first view. And then we got a second view and it's like, well, maybe he did. I don't I don't regret it. I mean, the call sheets's different from third and four to third and eight. Uh, you could argue like, well, was it really worth it for a four-yard game? Well, at that time of the game, it's early in the game. Uh, getting off the field was important to me, and I just happened to be wrong. >> Um, and then along those same lines, the fourth down and and going for it and knowing that they would get the ball back in your guys' territory. Um, just what did you see there in that play call with the the Quinn Sean run when you guys had been struggling on the ground? >> Yeah. Um uh I'm going to go for it again when we have inches to go. Um in that situation, we probably would have run the sneak, but after botching that, uh that wasn't an option. And and I don't I'm going to be aggressive. I'm going to play to win the game and and um and I'm more disappointed in our execution of it and our decision maybe uh in the the type of play, but I'm going to be aggressive if I don't want to give the ball back to them when it's when it's inches. We we have to be able to sneak it and we have to be able to to get it uh when um when when the you know when the opportunity arises. >> Next we'll go to Tony. Uh >> question on offense and defense. Todd, offensively, will you continue to use those modifications at practice to improve the operation? >> For sure. No, there was a difference there. There really was. We had a couple and some of those weren't wristband calls that we can certainly shorten and they were critical calls uh for Shawn, but really for the most part, our operation was better and it was cleaner. And defensively, when you came out for the warm-ups after the delay, Tyson Campbell did warm up, but he didn't play. Uh what's the state of him? And is it that did he get injured on that break up in the end zone or is this go back to the ankle? Well, he's he's got a number of things he's dealing with, but uh if I know Tyson, and he fought all game uh to continue to play, and uh if I know Tyson, he's going to work this week as hard as he can to get back. And we'll see as the week goes on where he's at, but I like I like his chance to be able to play based on how he's wired. >> Okay. Thank you. >> Next, we'll go back to Fred. >> All right, coach. Um, you got to be thrilled with the two rookies, Casey and Denzel, but how do you get Jerry Judy involved? It seemed like, you know, are they taking him away or, you know, with the other that he could really be, you know, another big explosive possibility there? Well, it kind of falls into kind of what we talked about last week is the moment that Jerry gets more targets, you're all going to be asking me why isn't Harold or you know then why isn't KC there's only one football and whether it's we certainly and the opportunities arose for all of those guys because we were struggling to run the football uh as effectively as we need to. And when that rises and we're better at that then Quinn Sean's going to have more carries, right? Right. And that's going to be less opportunities for the outside guys and Jerry's opportunities will come. It just like I said um a little bit by game plan and others that the ball just didn't find him. >> Okay. Thank go back to Mary Kay. Uh yeah, Todd, when we um talked to Denzel Boston after the game, he was talking about how um how Deshawn gave him an alert on the uh on the touchdown pass and uh and just kind of how those guys communicated that and Deshawn changed the play. Uh just wondering how um beneficial is it to you to have somebody that can do that at the line so effectively and then how about the communication that's growing between those guys? >> Well, we had it built into the play for a certain look. So they just communicated uh the play to change it. Uh the one that we missed on they uh they communicated a fade ball, you know, in the red zone uh that they almost hit. I mean, that was that was really that was a change of of of route that uh we came close to hitting. So, I'm I'm proud of their communication. I'm proud uh that our guys are dialed into the quarterback. Uh because again, you're never going to be as elite on offense if you don't empower your quarterback. Uh they're the guys on the field. >> Be Scott. Hey Todd, with uh Miles Harden, it looked like he had a pretty big bounceback game from week one. What did you see um out of him, especially on that interception? >> Well, he had a great week of practice. And Miles is a very prideful player. I mean, you don't get to where you're at, you know, and and a self-made player not be prideful and try to clean up some of the some of the little things from the week before. And um I thought he responded well last week in practice and and you can see it on tape and and every week's a little bit different. The matchup's a little bit different uh each week and but I'm happy for him to get the interception. Uh made another big play in the end zone. Um you know, so happy for him. >> And did you get a lot of reaction to your uh walk off the line last night? >> Uh I wouldn't say a lot of reaction. I mean I mean I did get a lot of text messages which was really cool. Uh some of it included that but um no not really. >> All right we'll wrap up with Cam Tony and Joe. Cam you can go first. >> Todd you mentioned last night uh just in that first half the the penalties that you guys had to to work through obviously clean it up in the second half. So, was that something that you guys you feel like you did specifically? Was that just product of the game? And and what does that look like moving forward to week three to try to clean up those penalties? >> They'll look at the same thing. And where we've struggled is when we've had large charted plays or penalties. There's been other things we've struggled at, but that's even in the second half on the drive we didn't score. We had a nice plan first down to get a first down and then we ran the ball and got a four- yard loss. And then we had a chance to hit Jerry Judy on the left side and he slipped. And so, you know, then the other drives when we didn't go backwards, we gave ourselves a chance. And first drive we get a nine yard gain and then we hand off a sweep and we lose six. Like, all right. So, and then we get a pretty good play on a power, you know, run in the red zone, we get a holding call, right? like it just felt like that we went backwards at times and that really put us behind the sticks and that's not a good I mean that's I mean in order of you know if you're going to what wins games being explosive don't turn it over uh lost yardage plays conversion downs touchdowns in the red zone and off schedule plays by your quarterback like that's that's what wins and one of them is lost yardage plays and if you probably if you look at what we did better on defense is the third down rates. Like we were better because we didn't have such a the long yardage and we were better on defense because they weren't always third and one or third and two. And so those lost yardage plays that gives yourself a chance on defense and it gives ourselves a chance on offense to eliminate those. And when we do that, we'll be a lot cleaner. >> Thank you, >> Tony. All right. Now, serious question. How much are you hoping >> are you saying Tony that the other questions were not >> No, I'm just saying you'll get my point when you hear this question. >> All right. >> How much are you hoping that the quarterback position becomes consistent enough that you're not asked who's playing quarterback week to week? And do you think Watson could convince us that it's a moot question? >> That is a serious question. You were right, Tony. you were right. Uh yeah, do I do I love dealing with it every week? Of course not. You guys keep asking. Uh which is a lot of fun. Um but the reality is of course, of course. And um you know, I'm happy for Deshawn the way he's played and I expect an improvement and I expect continued improvement. I mean there's a lot of um there's a lot of football left in him. just hasn't played in a while. And um and learning our system and trying to get him consistent with his drops and his reads is part of the process. He's like every player. I see him as a young player. I know people don't want to see it that way and and I haven't been here, but I see him as still a very young player that is going to continue to grow. >> All right. Very good. >> All right. We'll close out with Joe. >> Todd finishing out with two questions. Deshawn has said often that he hasn't been able to show what he's the full capability of your offense through two games. How much do you think you guys have shown or put in so far? I think some of it is Well, some of it's you know, he hasn't played in a while, right? I mean, that's a part of it. Part of it is a new system. Part of it is we can certainly call it better. Part of it is the players, like I said, players around it calling it better. New system. He hasn't played in a while. Like I would hope that we would continue to get better collectively. I would hope that's the case. I mean, in anything that you're doing and there's a lot of things we all need to clean up, coaching and playing. And that's you guys hear me say it all the time. I mean, you know, I believe in all of our players. I believe whoever we put on the field gives us a chance to win and that we can help them uh maximize their measurable skill set. That's that's what we're paid to do as coaches. And so, um, I'm anticipating, um, that that he'll continue to improve just like the other thing is while we were doing the quarterback competition, he split reps with the ones for a while and that benefited Shador, but it it maybe didn't benefit the guy that ended up being the starter. There's no way around that. I mean, that's that's that's obvious uh that you want to get the guys reps with the guys you're playing with. And um, I I was happy for Deshawn. He was our offensive player of the game. He made a number of plays with his legs, played with confidence, he let it rip. You could see the difference from week one to week two. And um I think we're just going to continue to grow together. And then in your wildest dreams or uh strangest bingo cards, did you ever have a first NFL coaching win the way everything went down, including a delay that ended up being only nine minutes longer than it took to play the baseball game here yesterday? Um, I don't know. I've been doing this long enough to to not really to say that I would think that's how it would go or how the game would go. I don't I don't know that. I know that we did the best job we could during that break to keep our guys focused, to keep them motivated, to try and let them know we're in the driver's seat. I know they're on the 28 yard line. I get that. But we're up a touchdown. and they still got to get in the end zone. This isn't a field goal game. And so to me, I asked him, I said, "Where would you rather be? Rather be us or them with our defense, they got to get in the end zone. Where would you rather be?" And to a man, it's like, "I'd rather be us." That's exactly right. Now go out there and do it. Shut them down. Let's let's and then let's get on the plane and get back home. And I'm really proud of the guys. This isn't about me. It's never has been wherever I've been. It's about the players. It's a players game. And we got a lot to clean up. coaching and playing and we took a giant step from week one to week two. So that'll be the message we come back Wednesday is so what? Now what? Like are we willing to take that same jump? I mean or or is it now all of a sudden uh we've arrived cuz it's week to week. You guys saw the scores. You guys know how this goes. Every team's a different matchup and we didn't turn the ball over which helped us in that first game. We turned it over two of the first board drives. So, it's basically, you know, so what now what are we going to do this week to continue to improve and we got the right guys to do it. That's what I love about our group because they're going to be ready to go to work on Wednesday. >> All right. Thanks, coach. >> And we'll have players around 3:45. Thanks.

title: Todd Monken & Deshaun Watson Press Conference | September 13th, 2026
text: And, uh but I'm I'm not I'm I'm not going down that road. I'll have enough time to go down that road watching the tape uh the way our guys battled and and finished the second half. I mean, so proud of our guys. That that's that's a win for our players. It's a players' game, and our guys made plays and had a great week um trusting the process, believing um that it's a week-to-week league. And we didn't put our best foot forward last week, and that's what's going to happen when you don't. And uh we played a lot cleaner this week. And uh not perfect, but I'm I'm going to enjoy this win for our guys. Um you know, this this is again, this is a players' game, and they make it go. And uh all they've ever done since I've been here is uh exactly what I've ever asked them to do in terms of their work ethic, in terms of every single day that we've asked them, and they've let me be me, which is uh really cool. >> Todd, what did everybody do during the delay when this was going on? >> We fueled. We hydrated. We played music. They kept their vibe up. We said, "We are in the driver's seat. We're up by I need a touchdown. We're in the driver's seat, and I told them, 'There's no other group I'd rather have out there than our defense to close it out.' Cuz that that's where we're at. After last week, which I said I wasn't going to go there, but after last week and how hard they played and the job they did to be able to close it out, uh that was awesome. >> What can you say about the game that Deshaun Watson had today? >> I mean, he played his rear end off in the second half, and he's doing it really without us running the ball very well, which is which we certainly are going to do better there. I mean, that that starts with me uh schematically and then calling it uh cuz that's hard. That's hard to win uh when you can't control the line of scrimmage and you can't comfortably uh turn around and hand the ball off. And um but Manny made some really nice plays with his legs, man. That the first third and one that he got it to Harold that extended the drive. There's a couple other plays he made with his legs. Um I thought he was in control, not perfect. And none of us are. I mean, I no one's ever going to make more mistakes than I make. I promise you. There's a lot of decisions I have to make and as the head coach and uh we're not mistake-free. We're human. And when we do that, just like we did last week, uh we own it and we fight like hell to fix it. And I'm I'm very happy for Deshaun. And uh I'm happy for us and the team uh for him to There's nothing like a locker room after a win. I don't care. There's no drug, alcohol, nothing that makes you feel like when you win as a team. And uh >> We We have to ask you this question. Is he the starter at home against Carolina? >> Really? >> I I don't know. >> Really? I'm going to enjoy this win. I mean, and I thought he played his ass off. I'm so happy for him. I'm just going to leave it there, right? I mean, good for him. Good for 22 months of working his off to get to where he's at. I'm I'm going to leave it at that. I'm so happy for him. This This is a player's game, man. There's nothing like the locker room. >> So, what kind of change did uh the approach to the run game in the first half make just in terms of how you got the ball to the passing offense? It did a little more for you. >> Just got the ball out of our hands. Just get the ball out of our hands. They were pressuring us and some of our other centers stopped and trying to throw it down the field and we just said we're going to get it out of our hands. And you know, and that was without a run game, you know, and they did a good job taking that away. I mean, I'm a big Todd Bowles fan, man. I'm a big Todd Bowles fan. I'm not a big fan of what the frick's going on here, but I'm a big fan of Todd Bowles. Okay? I I just am. And he really tests you and they you know with the pressures they gave and and we certainly can be better than that. But I thought Deshaun did a good job of distributing the ball. And in the first half we had lost yardage plays and penalties. We had holding calls and we didn't convert when we had opportunities and some of that's players and some of it's coaching. And that's what this game is. It's a we thing. It's not a me thing. It's not a them thing. Uh we got to coach better and play better and we'll continue to do that as long as we trust the process and put in the work every week like they did this week. >> So Watson was able to get Boston the ball Anything surprise you >> Uh no other than we needed him to get the ball more. I mean is that what you're getting at Tony? That for God's sakes. >> What changed What changed with the defensive performance? Obviously giving up 34 points tonight letting up >> I don't know. I still got to watch it. You know, I mean it's a week-to-week league, you know. It's It just is. Just look at the scores, right? Just look around, man. And um we just went back to work. That's a credit to Rudy and his staff and our players. Right? Um Were they happy about uh the game last week? Was Rudy as a coordinator in his first game at how we played? Was I happy in my first game as a head coach the way we played? No. You know what they did? Pulled their big boy pants up and go back to work and fight like hell to fix it. And that's all you can do. And that's what they did. And that's what we're going to do. We're going to enjoy this win and we're going to go back to work and get ready for the Carolina Panthers. >> I do you had said that you know, you had Deshaun Watson's back and you put your faith and trusted him. Uh can you just kind of talk about why you know, why did you believe in him? Why did you believe that he had a game like this in him especially after what happened to you last week. >> Well, first off, um I believe in all of our players. I believe in all I believe in our staff. I believe in this organization and where we're headed. So, he just happens to be one of those pieces and whoever we put out there, I expect him to play well. And whoever goes out there, um offense, defense, they expect us to scheme it up and give them the best chance to be successful. That's That's what a team is. There's a trust on both ends of it. There's a trust that we're going to put our players in position to be successful and there's a trust that they're going to go and execute. And you know, so uh again, I'm very happy for Deshaun. And and for our team. He's just one piece of that. he he played better because I called it better and because our players played better around him. This isn't This isn't a one-man game. This is not. And it takes everybody and I'm super proud of our guys uh the week they put in um cuz that's all you can do. All that does is give you a chance. It doesn't guarantee anything. But if you don't put in the work and you don't pull your big boy pants up and fight like hell to fix it, it's not going to work. And you're not going to get better. And that's what we're going to continue to do. I got the greatest job in the world. I'm the head coach of the Cleveland Browns for God's sake, how cool is that? >> How do you got you talked about you you visualize what that locker room would be like. After the first win, you you said it before you before this season started, you talked about visualizing that. How did it live up to what you had visualized you know, before it actually happened? >> Again, it's not about me. It It It's never has been. It's about the players. And uh it's always going to be way. I'm happy for them cuz they put in the work. I shouldn't say that. We all put in the work as coaches and players alike. Uh this is a tough this is a tough business. But that's why we get paid a lot. I mean it you better pull it again all of us, you know, man up when it's not good enough. And it wasn't good enough last week by me. There's a lot of things today that weren't and I'm going to go back to work, figure out how we can be better. But that there there's nothing like that. If you've ever been part of the team there's nothing like a celebration after a win. There just isn't. It's everything everything you do this for. Everything. >> Coach, at any point during the 2 hours did you want to punt? >> Well, a little bit cuz at some point you're like we're either going to be in 4-minute or we're going to be in 2-minute. And there's only so many calls you got. I really didn't think it would get down to where we'd have victory. I did I didn't think that. I thought we'd get a an earlier stop and we'd have to be in 4-minute or we'd have to in 2-minute. And then we got together with our skill guys and we talked about, you know, just like there at the end we talked about all the plays we needed if we needed chunk plays cuz it could have happened there, right? Hey, get the touchdown. Like how are we going to advance the ball and get it somewhere so our coaches did a great job of taking that information to our players cuz that's all you're doing. You're prepping for what ifs. That's all you're doing. So we hydrated, we fueled, got our guys ready to go, played music, you know, um talked about how cool it's going to be, right? You know, to close it out that way and uh our guys did it. And they backed up uh their preparation in there and we went out there and and uh got it done. >> Coach, what do you think it says after what you already talked about kind of the message to the group during the 2 hours? What does it just kind of say about I mean that that outcome could have gone a number of different ways after a long break like that and everything. What does it say that they, you know, kind of got through that and were able to overcome it and finish it off? >> Well, we needed it. Right? There's only so much you can talk about things in life, right? Ultimately, we're judged by wins and losses as coaches, and we're judged how we play on the field, right? It's not the name on the back. Player's name on the back is based on how they play on the field, not their history, not what they've done in the past. It's what you do every It's the same as us. At this point now, it's all about winning, and it's them about winning their matchups and the players on the field. That's That's what it's all about. It's At that point, it's you out there, and it's us collectively together. And I thought our guys did a great job of hanging together. We had We had a couple scuffles Wednesday, which is good. That's awesome. Cuz guys didn't like it, right? They're a little pissed off, right? You got to be a little pissed Played awful. It wasn't the standard. Browns are going to Browns. that. Okay? So, but the guys took that to heart. Thank you. >> Uh I don't know. You know, my my I'm just happy we got the win for real. >> Can you kind of sum up those emotions because you know you know, the the ups and downs and everything. You know, you you you you you've been kind of on front street about you know this journey you've gone on. Just what does it mean to finally you know, get back out there and get you know, get the win? >> Uh you know, right where I'm supposed to be. And you know, um leave the journey in God's hands. Keep working hard and keep pushing forward you know, let the outcome be the outcome when it comes. >> How much was the second half today exactly where you wanted to be as a quarterback >> Uh it was good. Just making plays. Told them Monk just to you know, trust me with the ball in my hands and and let me just go out there and just operate um and let him just, you know, scheme up, call the plays and and I'm going to trust his his mindset and um let's go execute. >> How good does it feel to go home going into that game next week coming off something like this, performance like this, given some of the stuff in the training camp? >> Oh man, honestly, I'm just happy with this win. So, right now I'm focused on right now and uh enjoying this win with my my teammates and honestly, I'm ready to go see my family. So, that's all I'm focused on. >> What did you guys do during the 2-hour >> Uh we we went over some stuff. Um the end of game kind of things. So, baby. >> Hi. >> Uh we uh you know, we went over some end of game, you know, process and and plays and then we just kind of hung out and just chill from there. Um no, I wouldn't I wouldn't say it was a topic of conversation. I just think that, you know, you know, Monk said what he said. So, that's how we all feel. >> Monk was talking about how like a couple stuff was one of the practices and like that's good that guys were saying that. I mean the results, how did you see the team bouncing back during the coming of the attitude >> I mean, the attitude was it was amazing. It was good. You know, you felt the energy. Guys want to win. Guys passionate. So, you know, it's going to it's going to be like that especially when you have your brothers in the locker room that, you know, is all together. So, um heck, man, even me and me and Monk went head-to-head a couple times. So, it was all good. It's all love, man. So, that's what you uh got to do to sometimes pull out a win like this. >> Do you feel like your back was against the wall and the stakes were very high for this game with what you know is going on at home against the Cowboys next week? Did you really feel like you had to dig deep and come up with a performance like this? >> No, man. >> What did you think about Boston today? >> Uh yeah, Boston is uh again a heck of a player, young guy that's that's keep improving each week. Him, Casey, uh just get the ball in their hands and make them. Uh but I I did get onto him on that that fade I threw him in the touchdown though, so Oh, most definitely. He He know that, too. So Yeah, he got to control that, but he uh we talked about it in that 2-hour break and uh you know, we're going to keep coming to him and keep giving him up those opportunities. >> Deshaun, you talked about your you know, you and Monk going at it. Just can you expand a little bit more on that relationship that you guys can have that you know, you can be with and building to try to push back and how he sort of pushed you and and believed in you in this >> Yeah, man. Our relationship [clears throat] it continues to grow every day. You know, the more we talk, the more we're around each other, the more we go through certain situations. you know, we're going to build that and you know, that's that's part of this game and and this league. You're going to have some ups and downs, you're going to go back and forth, you're going to agree to disagree, but at the end of the day we love each other, we got respect for each other, and that's what it matters. >> Deshaun, not much to talk about your just additional feeling of the world like being a locker room celebration for the win. >> Do you know what it is you wouldn't know that feeling as a starting quarterback? >> Nah. Nah, you tripping on that. I ain't never that. >> Deshaun, that play with Will Fuller that counted for a touchdown but obviously and just can you just talk about how that was? >> Yeah, it was good. I mean, we we kind of set that up. Uh my my stomach kind of dropped a little bit when he slipped. I thought he was about to fall, but uh that was something that we, you know, been working on and he did a good job of getting released in the backside and the O-line did a good job of protecting our backside and just get the ball to him and let him do the rest and we got a touchdown. >> How were you guys able to correct the operational problems from the last week? >> Big part of this week's >> Most definitely. Yeah, I mean, we cut down the the play clock. I know the play clock starts at uh 40 seconds, so we cut it down to 37, sometimes 35. The whole offense was on the sideline like we're in a real game. Uh usually we kind of stack behind each other on the plays, but uh we we put a big emphasis on that to make sure that operation wasn't going to, you know, deflect us from trying to get a win. >> We'll take three more. >> Yeah, every every week I'm getting more confident and more uh comfortable with myself. You know, I I got told Mark and I told the the team I feel good, I'm healthy. I trust the work that I put in these last 2 years and uh yeah, if you got to put the ball in my hands, I'm ready for it. So, um whatever we got to do to make the team win and and keep the drives moving, I'm ready for it. >> Deshaun Todd Todd kind of talked about what changed from the first and second half, trying to get the ball in your hands a little quicker and you talked about like telling Todd more than a trusting me. Just what did you kind of see in the first half that necessitated how how you guys kind of attacking the defense specifically? >> Yeah, I mean, I think we started off, you know, pretty good with heavy packages. Then they started coming out and adjusting on their end, uh bringing the the cat blitzes if y'all remember from Chicago. They were doing it with the Bears. Uh so, trying to pack the paint, so you know, we got in the gun and started operating from there. And uh letting our receivers work, getting the ball out quick and making them go side to side and I I that uh that helped us out and you know, so once they adjust, we adjust it. You know, it's just like boxing. You just keep going pound for pound until somebody give up and you know, we got the last one. >> It's the last one? >> How about the defense after a 2-hour and 12-minute rain delay? >> What was that? Oh, it was great. It was great. I mean, we were all together in there. We were hanging out on the golf cart. We were chilling, playing music, eating snacks. And, uh, yeah, we were just, you know, they kept coming to us on the offensive side like, "Hey, y'all did y'all job. Just know that we're going to handle our part, too." And, uh, and they kept their word and they did it, so it was a good complete team win and, um, it was great It's great to get a win in the, in this league. >> Appreciate it. >> Thank you. >> Woo! Woo!

Have you seen >> They're they're big and physical up front. They got a a really nice front. Um, they penetrate. Um, so it's going to be a big challenge for us. Um, their safeties are good players. They can tackle in space, cover ground. Um, so yeah, they're they're a good unit up front. Why is why is Craft your emergency tackle instead of Redmond or a defensive lineman? >> Yeah, [laughter] once you get to that option, there really is no good option. I was actually talking with some of the Dline coaches after the game and I'm like, we got to we got to find some Dlineman I think that could get in there, some backup guys that could get in there and help us out. So, uh yeah, unfortunately this isn't a good week to kind of explore that. Um, but yeah, we're we're going to be looking at some different options uh as we go forward, but it's good just to have a guy out there that kind of knows what direction to go uh for the most part. Uh when you put a D lineman in there, it could get ugly. So, um yeah, that that was a very scary situation. I was joking with Buckiss like you see uh Monks in the blue tent and he came out. It was like Undertaker popping out of the coffin. I was like, "Yes, [laughter] let's go." I was fired up because I was I was really scared at that moment. Um so that was good to see him. >> You've never seen him have a pass center tackle before, right? >> Uh that's happened when I was in San Francisco that happened where we had uh our tight end play. >> I'm talking about like you ever seen him pass? >> Well, yeah. Not at tackle, but I mean you watch the Minnesota game, he was pass blocking um a lot. So he he has plenty of experience doing that. Um that but obviously not something you want to live in for sure. >> You were you were not here when they played the >> Yeah. No coaching I was not but I remember coach gets he was talking about that after the game. He's like well we had to do it in the playoffs and I was like oh my god that would be awful. So yeah deal. >> Yeah that was that was rough >> on the sideline. >> Yeah it would be rough. >> How different is it pass setting at tight end to right tackle? Like it's one spot over right. For the uneducated eye, that's a huge difference. >> Yeah. I mean, it's just all about space. Like the further you go away from the center, the more space you have, but then you also just have to understand where you are in relation to where you think the quarterback is. You know what I mean? So, the it's just all about the the closer you get in, the faster you have to react, the more stout you have to be. So, yeah, it's just get on your guy and hold on at that point and just fight fight your butt off. Uh, yeah. Sorry to interrupt the reliving your nightmare. >> Um, but what did you think of what Jagger did in the 23 snaps and [clears throat] and is there you talk about continuity all the time. I know Banks is your left guard if he's healthy, but is there any talk about >> let's just figure out our five and go and go with the growing pains. >> Yeah, I think that would be great for sure. And we'll kind of see how it plays out this week. You know, if banks can go, great. If not, then we'll work those other guys in. And um for me, I just want to see whoever's in there just go make it hard for us to make a decision. You know what I mean? Like go out there, compete, be productive, be clean, eliminate penalties, uh and just make it really hard on us to take you off the field if you're one of those backup guys. That's that's really what I want to see. >> Speaking of Jagger, why did it take like two car wrecks in a plane crash to get him on the field? He went from rotating with Banks with the ones all summer and then all of a sudden it seemed like he was a last resort against the Jets. >> It wasn't really a last resort, but we had Donovan Jennings ahead of him in a in the rotation. Um, and then Donovan went down and then so Jagger went in. Um, and that was just kind of what we saw the last few weeks of camp. Um, I talked about this a couple weeks ago, just Donovan was playing better, Jagger wasn't. But that doesn't mean it's not, you know, we write that in pencil. It's not in pen. Um, and yeah, I I I liked what I saw from him. I'm talking about Jagger. Uh, he did a nice job out there competing, and I'm if he's playing, I'm excited to see him out there. I like all the guys. I thought their play style was nice. You know, we have a lot to clean up obviously. Uh, but they were playing hard and we can work with that for sure. Morgan specifically, what have you seen from him in terms of adjusting to left tackle these first two starts? >> Yeah, he's kind of he was going through some stuff. I think this last game um you you saw some better fundamentals with him. There was a few times uh he we got to get on the page with the snap count and stuff like that. We had some issues with that. So again, just the controllable things that we can control like coming off on the ball, things like that. We got a clean up because there was too many issues last game and we were lucky to get a win uh with with those things, penalties and whatnot. >> What do what do you do or what's your mindset when both your halfbacks fumble? I mean, is is your first inclination like I want to bench a guy and and so he understand >> No, I mean you you obviously get upset, but like they're not going out there trying to fumble, you know what I mean? like they everyone knows the expectation if you hand if we give you the ball what's the expectation is to protect it uh for the entire franchise. So that's it's just one of those learning moments. Hopefully they can learn from that and just be better with their ball security moving forward. Um but yeah the it wasn't just them. It was we had four fumbles. So obviously that's unacceptable. We can't have any fumbles. >> Was it was there commonality in how they were holding it or anything in those? I couldn't really see from one of the angles, but I know uh JJ did a really nice job punching that ball out uh on one of them. And sometimes, you know, if you he just catches you right and there's a little space in your elbow or whatever it is, that thing's coming out. And that was a good hit by him for sure. Um yeah, >> when you come off a game like that, when you do have all the fumbles and the number of drops in that game, are you allowed as a coach to say, "Well, you know, it's raining." >> No, >> but that's not acceptable. That is a >> comp. Yeah. I mean, that's a thing, but you practice every day in the elements, whatever it is. Like, you have to understand that that's football. That's what makes football great. Like, that's the great equalizer is the weather. Um, so no, there's no excuse for any of that stuff. >> Did you feel like, you know, Caleb gave you guys kind of a smart build? >> Yeah, he did. He did a nice job. He came in there, ran hard, and that's I told him, I just want to see angry runs. Go in there and just run hard, run angry. Um, and I thought he did a nice job with Um, Bill talked to Tim Lester a couple weeks ago and he said he basically xeroxed Matt's offense and installed as much as he could. Is Caleb in a place where he can give you even more because he's got some background? >> Yeah, there's familiarity there for sure. Um, you know, he he we definitely had those conversations when he came about some of the things that uh he was familiar with. So, yeah, that helped definitely. I know Jordan's never going to lead the league in completion percentage just because of, you know, the way he plays the game, put the ball down field, but he's last right now. How do you get that up to where you wanted to get to? >> Yeah, I think you know, one thing probably he'll tell you is just taking those easy completions and um you know, checking the ball down. I think that's one thing that we could do to and you saw it at the end of the game. He checked the ball down to Brooks. Brooks made a big play. Um so we got some good playmakers. We just got to get them the ball. Um and just trust your guys and they'll come through for you. Is that the fine line with him? He's so good at making >> Yeah, he's just aggressive. Like he wants to push the ball down the field. He wants to, you know, hit those vertical passes, but sometimes they're not there and you just got to check it down. >> Jordan plays the position the way he does by his own pass. He's had a lot of success that way. He's also talked about how there's probably more opport. I think it takes a game like this where they're like, "Oh, yeah. Okay, I got to remember to use my legs when they give it to me." And he's he's shown that he has definitely has the ability to do that. So, I'm not too overly concerned uh with that. But, yeah, it's just one of those things where you you go back and you watch the film, you're like, "Yep, I could have taken off here and gotten a big gain." So, again, him he's trying to be aggressive down the field. Um just got to see the big picture and make those plays when they give it to you. Is there a balance with that? Because his his cannon makes a lot of >> Yeah, I mean there's definitely you don't want to over coach it. It's just one of those things if you have a feeling and you want to take it, take it. But if not and they they have bad rush lanes or whatever it is, then yeah, go ahead and use your legs and make a play. >> I know there's no one answer to this, but to improve on third downs, how much of that is what's taking place on third down versus what's happening first and second? >> I think you hit it right there. We need to be more productive on first and second down to give us a chance. I think uh if you look at like third and seven and under, we're around 50%. And obviously, but we've just been third and eight plus it seems like every time. So, we need to do a better job on first and second down in order to take care of third down. Um so, yeah, that's that's the biggest problem in my opinion. I know you can't do this on a short week, but given the juggling along the offensive line, this is something you've done in the past as far as kind of switching up your approach in the running game. Uh, you know, when Malik came in a couple years ago, you guys got to some stuff that we hadn't seen a lot. >> Does that drive you to try and figure some other stuff out because you've got different body types in there? >> Uh, yes and no. I think right now, you know, we're just still trying to find kind of where we're at offensively. Um, so you don't want to get too crazy too fast. Um, but yeah, it's every game you're just kind of trying to take the next step forward. >> Good. All right, guys. Thanks. See you. >> Good luck. >> Thank you.

title: Head Coach Matt LaFleur Press Conference
text: This is good. Get here before everybody. >> Yeah, well, when did Van Ness and Hargrave end up in concussion protocol? >> Um Van Ness, Monday. Hargrave, yesterday. >> Is that just the residual effects of something that >> Apparently, yeah. >> Do you foresee it being anything long-term? >> I mean, I think that's always the magic question. You never know with a concussion. There's a That's why there's a protocol. >> Dan and I talked about how the importance of pressure from specifically the defensive tackle position. So, I was curious from an offensive perspective if there's steady push from the middle, just what extra challenges does that add for for an offense in that situation? >> Well, you can't Yeah, I think the number one thing is, first of all, it's very hard to throw with pressure internal pressure in your face. I mean, you typically got to move. And a lot of times, you know, you want a nice clean pocket where a quarterback can step up into the pocket. And when you get that internal pressure, that eliminates that possibility. >> They also seem to use tight ends like crazy. Um the Jets have What what challenges does that present? >> I think the more personnel groupings an offense possesses, just the more prep that goes into it cuz now you got to have multiple ways defend to defend all those different personnel groupings. >> Did you ever see five before with them the way they deployed that package? I think there was five at one point one of those snaps against them. >> Yeah, I I I I missed that one. That was JG. Hopefully, I'm sure he saw that one. >> How did Banks get through yesterday? >> He had he had a good day at work. So, hopefully he can get back out there today and continue to build upon that. >> Is that going to be a long thing you think where you know his availability is in doubt each week or >> You know, I think that's something that we'll find out in time. I'm I'm I sure hope not, but um unfortunately over the last couple of years I've learned that that's not always the case especially up front. We've had a lot of guys that have been in and out and um that's just the way it is. >> I know Trey has shown he's got an ability to make some long field goals. I think there was something I think Elias said that was the longest that any kickers have in his debut for 59 yards. Just how do you think he's handled that and just what has he shown you in terms of just the overall leg strength? >> Yeah, well I mean he's he's shown us exactly like who we thought he could be, but yeah, I think just I think it speaks to the confidence that he has in himself. Obviously we have a lot of confidence in him just to put him in those situations. Never want to put put a guy in that situation for his first kick, but uh done that a couple times now. So, you know, hopefully we can do a better job offensively to put him in a better position or just having kick PATs is what you really want, but um now he's he's done a great job, but as we all know, you're only as good as your last performance and he's got to continue to build upon these. >> When you have a steady running game to lean on specifically in the red zone, just what benefit can that do for the offense? >> Well, just keeps you on schedule, so you're not in those known pass situations and then you get more coverage heavy defenses typically uh that makes it a little bit more difficult to throw the football. >> Is it already a more difficult part of the field to throw just because there's less space >> absolutely. You get down in the red area, it that the coverage gets tighter, obviously. Um you know, there's just less grass to defend down the field vertically. Uh so, corners you know, can squat if it's a free access coverage. A lot of it kind of depends on the coverages. Um and then it's sometimes it's a guessing game because you could call a concept meant for one coverage, you get a different coverage and it looks absolutely terrible, gets gloved. And that's where you need your quarterback to be able to make those off-schedule plays. Um so, it's it's much more difficult in the red area. >> And the way that because of the way the Vikings game played out, you know, probably not able to run the ball as much as you would have liked to, but seeing the way Marshawn was able to get through that game and deal with the hits that he gave, does it give you a sense of confidence that, okay, this guy can take those carries? >> Yeah, I think he did he did a good job. And um it it's something to build on and I think we've been building I would say throughout the course of the off-season, throughout training camp into those preseason games and now we're here. So, hopefully we can just continue to build him up and um I think he's [snorts] he's shown a lot of confidence that he's able to do it and that gives me confidence. >> Hey Matt, you mentioned uh JJ yesterday. What kind of player and teammate was Enyobeni and um I mean, I remember actually one of his best games as a rookie was against the Jets. >> Yeah, I I I I think I got a lot of respect for JJ, just how he competes. I mean, he is a tough, gritty guy. Uh is able to set at hard edges in the run game and then get after the passer. So, I think he's a really versatile player. So, there you go. That's team to come together is tonight. I think I think it was a glimpse of it to be honest because I think we can we still got another level we can tap into and um I don't say that being you know try to try to be like that but at the end of the day I mean we take care of the ball a little bit better that you know that can equate to more points so this team I mean we got to the confidence level that we're at just because of the work that we put in and we understand you know that we don't we're not going to put any you know uh governors on what we can do here and at the end of the day we can go out and win that game and say we're we're obviously we're happy about it and we're thrilled to to win and it's a any win in this league is is one to celebrate but when you look back it's you know you're trying to be great and be a be a Super Bowl caliber team. Uh, god damn it. [laughter] But, uh, but yeah, it's when it when it's needed, anybody can come out and do it. Yeah, I think that was really one of the major uh pieces like the the the things that we wanted to, you know, be locked in on this week was just making sure we had fun. So, um I definitely don't take it lightly. >> On the FA ball to the end zone, what's going through your mind when you see the DB lineup inside and give you all that space? Yeah. Well, they I saw they were trying to double. So, I was wondering what was going on with the leverage and uh soon as the ball snapped, he didn't he didn't have the correct leverage. Um, just when you look back to a year ago when you guys hadn't had a lot of reps to this point, just from your end, how how much has it grown just in the past year? >> Yeah, I mean, we didn't get any time until the week leading up into week one last year. So, um, football is the the the greatest team sport that there is and, you know, it's it's it's a beautiful game because it takes so many things in order for things to go right and, um, you know, we can both be great players and go out there and have the right intentions every time and that doesn't, you know, it doesn't make sure that or that doesn't guarantee anything for you. So, we just try to be locked into the details as much as we can and we we've had a lot more time to work together and um, yeah, it goes out and it looks like that now. >> Just left the room. were in a real good zone tonight. Nearly 200 yards for him. What was your thoughts on Devonte performing? >> I thought he was outstanding. Um, obviously he's a fantastic player, has been for a long time in this league. We're lucky to have him on our team and, uh, you know, he played huge for us tonight. Obviously, Puka being down, um, you know, was a a big miss for our team. Um, so we leaned heavily on Dvonte and I thought he did an outstanding job really all week preparing to play and then obviously, uh, came out here on Monday night and did his thing. as a wider shoe on this team, but I think you know better that he's a wider super without question for him to be able to still show that at 33 years old, 13 years into his career. What does that say about about him? >> Yeah, I mean it's a testament to how he takes care of himself um you know and how he's done that for a long time. Um he's an elite player. He made all sorts of plays today. Made contested catches. He ran great routes and got open. He did it all for us. And uh he's a guy that can do that. We understand that. We know it. And uh like I said, leaned on him big time tonight and he he came through for us. Was there an obvious uh an obvious energy level difference this week? >> Yeah, I thought our guys came out played great. Um played with a bunch of passion, energy, excited to be back home in SoFi. Um you know, our defense led the charge, played fantastic, kept them out of the end zone and and obviously made some big plays, some turnovers, fourth down stops, those kind of things that we were able to rally on. Um you know, we did enough offensively. Still left some plays out there. We're a little bit um you know, not as efficient as I would have liked in certain areas. you know, just some plays that we can make that we didn't make. Um, and we do that, we'll like where we are, but it was nice to get a win, you know, kind of as we're as we're finding a way to be >> Matthew on Thursday passing touchdowns, when you see the names that you're passing, what does that kind of mean to you about where you put yourself in? >> Well, where I've put myself doesn't feel right to say. I got I got to throw those to guys, you know, I got to have guys that, you know, are blocking um, you know, for me and helping me, you know, get to where that is. But, uh, I am a huge fan of this league, have been since I was a little kid. And, um, to be mentioned in, you know, the same light as some of the guys that I grew up watching and idolizing and wanting to be like, and then getting the chance to compete against some of those guys as well. It it it's a special feeling. Um, you know, this game is a special game. It's it's treated me and my family and my life uh, you know, really well. So, just happy to be, you know, a part of it and have so much respect for those guys that did it before me. >> As quarterback of this team, what was it like to see that guy back? I was so juiced. Um, he came running out of the tunnel and I couldn't control myself. I was freaking fired up, man. I don't know if y'all, y'all, I'm sure y'all are in there, but man, the fans were happy to see him back and and we all were, too. Just listen, just the human being, the player, all of it combined. Uh, what he brings to our team and to our locker room is unmatched and really to the city, which I thought was amazing. U, I thought it was a great reception for him tonight. Obviously, welld deserved. talk about the trust that you have one when Kiran fumbles you go right back to him when Terrence has like the the trust you have >> Yeah I mean for us to be our best we need everybody and it's it's a full team effort and listen nobody's perfect we all have plays that we want back um you know I put one in harm's way today as well so um I I just want the best for those guys you know I'm hard on some of those guys sometimes and it's only because I believe in them and I want the best for them so uh they all know that I think Shawn does a heck of a job of believing in those guys as well which is a really cool feeling um you know for those guys to be believed in because it's authentic and it's true. Listen, we need everybody. We trust everybody. They're out there for a reason because they've earned the opportunity to be out there. Um, you know, and they're and they're going to help us, you know, at some point down the road. So, >> what are you doing? >> Past your bedtime [laughter] >> right now, y'all. But it felt good to be back out there, man. Um, get that first game under my belt, you know. you know, felt like it as it started going on. It's kind of slowed down at, you know, towards the third and fourth quarter, but um got it under my belt officially back playing football. You know, came away with a win. So, I'm excited about that. >> When you came out of the tunnel, it was surreal for so many people. You being in that moment, coming out of the tunnel, hearing your name. What did that feel like for you? >> Um, I did a little bit more jumping than I usually do. So, it kind of amped me up a little bit, man. It felt good, you know. It felt good to be back coming out. um being embraced how it was. So, it was definitely special. >> How much did it help you being back out there and be able to have the energy that you have and disseminate that amongst your fellow brother on the defensive side? >> Well, it's great cuz guys was flying around, man. Um I think the defense played great stuff to run. Guys were getting out to the quarterback. By made some big plays. Um Kobe Fist, them guys was just flying around. So, um I think today the defense played, we played how we pose to play. Um always got room for improvement, right? Um so, um it was a good start, good win. um enjoyed the day and right back to work tomorrow. >> Did you ever catch yourself going, "Dang, I really am here." >> No, I was more like I gotta get myself going. You know, you feel a little rust, you know, at times rushing got a little high, but you know, I I I'll clean them things up first game back. Um more important is is getting the win, you know. Um and that's what it's all about, right? Finding ways to win. >> I'm sorry. Think of the two words, rust and also speed. Speed of the game. How much did that take a little time to say, "Wait a minute, this we haven't done this in a while." >> The game really wasn't as fast as I, you know, thought. It was more of me calming myself down, right? Um, you know, overrunning stuff or just being my feet not being in the ground how they supposed to be, not trusting my eyes, little stuff like that. But, you know, playing the game when I held out in 17, 18 was the same way. When I came back, it took a couple games to get going. It's a little different. I ain't playing two years. So, um, you know, I got to watch the film, see what I did good, see what I did wrong, and and just clean it up. So, but we won. >> Harris. Did that feel familiar? >> Yeah, it felt good. You know, it felt good. It would have been better if I was able to slam him though. But, you know, but again, first game back, we get there. >> Did you ever feel like, why did I even leave? This is a lot of fun for me. >> Um, you know, when you in the moment, you don't think about that. You know, like I said, once I started to get back playing football, I kind of felt like I was never gone. You know, it kind of felt like I played last year. You know, you you don't until you be like, "Dang, I really didn't play football in two years." you just in the moment um you know with the guys in the locker room and just trying to prepare you know trying to win a game >> with the offense catching fire the way that they did just how fun was it for you guys to really just be able to get after the quarterback? >> It was great. It was really good see how they was rolling get going um doing great in the first half but second half kind of you know took over. So um that's what it's about. It's about team football finding ways to you know win as a team and we did that today. >> How humbling is it? How humbling is it to walk away from this game and to come back and hear Matthew say the human the human being is who we like in the locker room. This is not the team you left Aaron. That's how I move. Um you know I I just I just work right. That's all I can do. Find ways to get better. Try to embrace guys that's around me. you know, and hear guys that like Matthew Stephfords and guys that I respect and I look up to um that played this game a long time at a high level, you know, to hear that type of stuff is definitely, you know, it feel good to hear. You know, >> it's just a little sore, man. I just said I'm sore. I ain't play Two two two padded practices and then a game like you know what I'm saying? >> You're confident smacking. >> You're confident the other >> last two. >> You're confident the other day that you wouldn't see double teams after two years off. Um, I felt I felt the love, you know, I felt the play and they and I, you know, I made that little tackle for loss and, you know, um, hear the fans saying, whatever they were saying, it felt good, you know. title: Lions at Bills Week 2 | Detroit Lions Live CURE Auto Insurance Postgame Show
text: Welcome to the Detroit Lions live postgame show presented by Curado. I'm Brooke Kirchoffer alongside Super Bowl champ and Lions legend Lis Brown. The final score from Buffalo 41-31 in favor of the Bills. Lis, it seemed to be that the Lions just ran out of time. And how frustrating it is when you put put up 31 points on the road to a really good team, but it's after that first quarter, the Lions just seemed to be behind the eight-ball trying to catch up to this Bills team. >> Yeah, Brooke, the thing that you can't do in this league, you cannot have self-inflicted wounds. You can't have the penalties. You can't stop drives because of things that you're doing, especially when you're going up against good team. Well, great teams like Buffalo and great quarterbacks like Josh Allen, we didn't take advantage of trying to keep their offense on the sideline and it really really hurt us. But I thought the one thing that hurt us the most were the penalties that we got um in the game. >> Really just a frustrating start to this one. But again, we still saw a fight from the Lions. Let's go ahead and get to those penalties. Looking at the stats from the from this matchup for the offense. Nine penalties with a beat up offensive line. A lot of those penalties coming from the offensive line. Lom miss. Larry Borum stepping in for Blake Miller. And that really seemed to be, excuse me, 10 penalties for the final there. We saw that one right at the end as we were getting set up here. 10 penalties really was the killer for the Lions. >> Yeah, it really was. And again, you can't have things like that. And it's not the amount of penalties. Well, I guess it is the amount of penalties, but it's when they happen. And it seems like all our penalties happen when we're in good position to pick up third downs. And a lot of those penalties, Brooke, they were pre- snap penalties. And those are the one that drive coaches crazy because those are penalties that you can avoid. Those are the penalties that you don't need through the game. So, I'm quite sure Dan is going to be quite upset about this and it's going to be an emphasis going into this week of practice. >> It was another slow start for the offense, too. We saw just how crucial it is to get Junior Gibbs going early. They couldn't really struggle to run the ball. Meanwhile, for Buffalo, their offense was humming in their home opener, I think, feeding off of a new stadium. The crowd atmosphere on that first drive alone, Lis 63 rushing yards on that Buffalo's first drive. And then of course on the second drive, we saw the busted coverage from the defense. Guy left wide open. And of course, anytime Josh Allen sees a guy wide open like that, he's going to punish the defense. Their offense was just clicking at every level. >> It really was. And what happens, Brooke, when their offense is clicking like that, guess what? Our defense is on the field a lot more. And you start wearing out the defense a lot earlier. Don't forget, our defense played 91 plays versus the Saints. And then to come in here early into this game and have to play a lot of games, it really just a cumulative effect of it. It really wears you out. So again, I know coach has put a lot of emphasis on the offense. The offense has to be the catalyst of this team until we can get important guys back on the defensive side of the ball. >> Absolutely. We did see one bright spot was when Jir Gibbs was not able to run the ball as effectively behind that injured offensive line when he got into the passing attack. How that opened things up. The three receptions for over 30 yards. Very impressive to watch. But let's get to the defensive side of the ball. Jared Goff really did not have a whole lot of time to throw. That is a credit to this Bills defense that was without Ed Oliver. They were still able to affect Jared Goff. He did not have a whole lot of time. Meanwhile, for Josh Allen, Aiden Hutchinson got to Josh Allen at times, but as we see, he can dazzle with his feet and keep plays alive, and that's what he did to start this. >> You're right. And anytime we lost contain, it gave Josh Allen the opportunity to get outside, buy even more time to let his receivers get downfield or for him to use his legs if he wanted to. So, you're right. It was it it was a a thing where we knew coming in here what type of player we were going to face, how we were going to have to be disciplined going up against a Josh Allen. It just didn't work out early for us. I think it kind of compounded things to where we just couldn't get back into the game the way we needed to. >> And you see Jared Goff, five sacks. Really, they were all over him tonight. He struggled to really have time to throw as we mentioned, but credit to this Bill's defense. They came in with a game plan. We saw that chess match between their defense and Drew Ping who's still trying to figure out this offense. >> Yeah. And the one thing that I've seen, Brooke, is now I'm looking at teams now, this is second week in a row. They're forcing us to throw the ball to the perimeter, but throw it short. We haven't been able to take shots downfield. And I know that's the defenses are coming in and they're preventing us from doing that. So some type of way, shape, or form, but we're going to have to be able to stretch this ball downfield or the only thing's going to happen, those safeties are going to start coming closer and closer to the line of scrimmage. Then you won't be able to run the ball because it'll be too many guys in the box. So, we're going to have to get our passing game going, but it's going to have to be longer passes to make the defense respect us going over their head. >> Meanwhile, our secondary continue to get picked apart. Of course, we saw Levante Maddox left the game with an injury. Rocky with a bit of a banged up situation at the end of this game. We will keep an eye on that as we get ready now for week three. But what did you see from that side of the ball and how really our secondary struggled against Josh Allen's attack? Yeah, they're gonna struggle because one, we weren't really getting to Josh Allen. What we have to do, as you know, Brooke, the pass rush in the secondary, they're tied at the hip. If we can get a pass rush on it, it gives the quarterback less time to look downfield or it gives the the receivers less time to let their routes develop. When they when Josh Allen is able to buy time and extend the plays, then it puts so much more pressure on your secondary to try to cover up these receivers. And as we know, these receivers are very good in this league. >> Yes, they are. Let's get to the quarterback comparison heading into this matchup. Josh Allen and Jared Goff lead the NFL in explosive offenses for the last five seasons. That's saying something. And when you look at the numbers between the two of them here, I mean, not the worst day for Jared Goff. 26 of 38 with 327 passing yards. But Lomus, we know that sometimes is a stat that is a little bit lopsided. It's because they could not run the ball as effectively. >> You're exactly right. Sometimes stats can be misleading. And I do think if we were able to run the ball and run it consistently, then I could look at that being a little different. But you're right, a lot of that Jared Golf was under distress. A lot of those were short passes. It would be interesting to see the distance of some of Jared Goff is the average distance of his passes because I thought Buffalo did a great job, but like I say, making us check things down and show throwing the shorter passes. >> Let's highlight that time of possession because I think that's an underrated statistic and the ability that Josh Allen has to be a game manager. Third quarter, an 8 minute and 30 second drive was the killer for the for the Lions. They just did not get the ball back in time to be able to eat at this lead. >> Absolutely. And to to compound the problem, they went eight minutes plus they put it in the end zone. At that point, we needed to hold them to a field goal to try to get back into the game. So, it was kind of a double-edged sword. They took time off the clock and then they punched it in the end zone to increase their lead. Uh you just have to give Buffalo a lot of credit. They came out ready, especially defensively. I thought they played very well defensively cuz they held us down for pretty much most of the game. >> This is one get ready for week three. Yeah, >> it's a little it's the ex it's a short by week for them, right? With a Thursday night matchup. We'll see how they get back to the drawing board. And first, we'll hear from head coach Dane Campbell who's at the podium now. >> All right. Give them credit. Uh, you know, Joe Brady, uh, had those guys ready to go. They played well, uh, you know, all three phases and, uh, they got after us and we didn't we didn't play good enough and and we didn't coach good enough. you know, that falls on me. And uh you know, we we just we we needed to play a uh it didn't have to be spotless, but it certainly uh needed to be a lot cleaner than that, and we did not do that. And uh we needed we knew we needed to score some points. Um we uh we stalled out early in that game. You know, that that got us early. You know, you're down three scores and really we haven't done anything offensively. And so a lot of that help needed to come there um to be able to answer back um so we fell short there. title: Saints WR Devaughn Vele on Tyler Shough, offensive playmakers and HC Kellen Moore's trust in players
text: I, I give Shaka credit, you know, he was very mature from the start.  He doesn't have many starting games at quarterback, but he's doing a great job of it.
