I mean, obviously Taisem Gill is out for a while, but between you, Chris Olave and Juvan Johnson.  Do you think everyone he passes the ball to is capable of making an explosive play? Yes, of course.  I think this team is very balanced.  I believe we have talented players at every position.  We have great running backs, tight ends, receivers, and the offensive line creates opportunities.  I think resources like that help Shaq feel confident, and when he's confident, he makes big plays. What do you like about the diversity of our offense? What exactly? Regarding the diversity of our attack in this aspect. Yes, of course.  As I said, it's great because everyone has their strengths, we're all different, and when the situation calls for a certain player to show off, we have someone who can do it.  I think this has become the key to the success we are achieving now.  So we'll just continue to build on that success. It didn't quite translate into a lot of points in the first half of yesterday's game, but the offense performed better than it did last week.  Why is this so? I think it's a matter of getting off to a quick start, which is what we always talk about .  At the same time, this is one of those games where you have to continue working methodically. Look for weaknesses in the defense, understand what they do, their schemes and all that.  And when you start taking small successful actions, it opens up opportunities for big productive moments.  And that's exactly what we saw when CD Lamb and Juwan made those important plays when we needed it most. Having performances like this against teams that could potentially be rivals at the end of the season, what does it mean for all of you? Oh, that's a great indicator, I guess, of what stage we're at now as a team.  Of course, we have things to work on. Of course, we have to watch the replay and see what to build on from there, but I think it's a good step in the right direction that helps build the confidence that we need, because we want to be big and achieve a lot this season.  I think we are capable of this. And if we continue this thought, then such a victory makes the city buzz. How excited are you to return home, to the arena, and feel this passion of the fans? Oh, that's just wonderful. It will be nice to come back.  Yes, being away for the last two weeks has been a bit difficult, but it will be great to be home again with our fans and feel their support.  So we are happy to be back. Sorry if you've already answered this, but what Kellen entrusted you with winning the game on a two-point conversion last week, and on fourth down in the end zone this week. How confident is he in you that you can go out and win the match?  And what feelings does this evoke in you ? This is simply incredible. I really like that Kellen trusts us so much .  I wouldn't even call it a risk. I think it shows his confidence in his team and the guys he has .  This helps us believe in ourselves, because we know that the coach believes in us.  So we have to do everything to make his faith justified, you understand?  So I feel very grateful to him for that.

title: Can the Jets Make a STATEMENT in Home Opener vs. Packers?
text: The Jets and the Packers Sunday in the home opener at Metife Stadium. The Jets Collective is here to preview the matchup. It starts right now. [music] It's our second episode of the Jets Collective. That's because in season we're moving to two episodes per week. My name is Jake Amin, joined as always by Ritz Camini and Brandon Tierney. Thank you to everyone who watched our Monday night episode as of this taping. Over 22,000 views. So to everyone who tuned in, thank you. Make sure you're liking the video, subscribing to the channel. If you haven't, BT, Rich, we got ourselves quite the football game on Sunday. BT, how we feeling? >> Well, well, first of all, we're feeling great. But hold on now, Rich, I'm going to You got to help me out with this. All right. Ready? Happy birthday [laughter] to Jake. to Jake. >> Happy birthday to Jake. Happy birthday to Jake. Happy birthday to you. 31 years old. Happy birthday. And you are the young buck on the show. So, Jets coverage will be in your hands a lot longer than the other two on the show. And it's and it's in good hands. Happy birthday, buddy. >> Thank you, guys. Hopefully, one of these years we're we're covering a a winning team. But hey, for at least week one, we certainly got that. I joked with Rich off air that Rich has covered the Jets longer than I've been alive. So I it is >> Yeah, thanks for that, Jake. Appreciate that. [laughter] >> Yeah, it was a joke. I don't think Rich laughed that much and I wouldn't have either. [laughter] >> Uh to be young again, but uh you know what? Uh despite my age, I I am excited about this game on Sunday. This is uh Hey, look, let's face it. The Jets haven't been 1 and 0 that often in their history. I think they've only been 2 and 0 11 times out of 66 years of history. So, if they could get if they could win the game on Sunday, what a boost that would be and they'd be kind of rarified air for this franchise. >> If you're watching the show live again, click the thumbs up button, subscribe to the channel, shout out to Prize Picks for being our presenting sponsor. You know, Rich, 2 and 0 is such a unique thing in the NFL. There was a study that Rotoire did where dating back to 2016, so this is a 10-year sample size, that teams that start 2 and 0 make the playoffs 66.6% of the time, basically 2/3. So, I'm not saying if the Jets win Sunday, they're a playoff team. But, it does go to show you getting off to a good start has major impact for the type of team you could potentially be down the stretch. >> Uh, it's just it's just so big for your confidence. And I could feel it in the locker room this week talking to players. I mean, they they kicked Tennessee's tail on Sunday and they know it and they they enjoyed it and that just does so much because demonstrated ability, I think this is a Parcel's quote, some there's nothing like demonstrated ability that inflates one's confidence level. And uh you could I could just sense it in the locker room, the way players are moving, the way players are talking. Uh they sound like a 1 and0 team. They sound like a very confident team that they can beat Green Bay on Sunday. We'll dive into that in a little more detail, but uh yeah, 2 and 0 would be a big lift for the entire Aaron Aaron Glenn program. >> Yeah. I mean, think about this, guys. I think that this applies to anything in life. Like if if you golf and you whatever that benchmark might be, I'm trying to break a 100, try to break nine. Until you actually do it, you don't feel great getting out of the car going on to the first T- box. Like doing an experience, it's a galvanizer. And I don't care what you espouse and how animated the meetings are and how good the practices are until you feel and experience that tangible success which in the NFL is obviously a win. You know, it's it's going to be a little less that it's going to be a little hollow. So, I love that Rich said that he can feel it a little bit more palpably in the locker room and they should because they didn't just Now, the Titans stink. We and we did this on Monday. We know Tennessee is going to be maybe with the Dolphins and with the Browns among the worst three teams in football, we would think, right? But they didn't just win like 13-6 or seven 10-7. They kicked the crap out of them. They owned them at the line of scrimmage. They protected their quarterback. The game call, the play calling offensively was on point. The tackling was hard. The special teams was locked in. There's a lot to take away from that and uh they should be feeling good because they look great. Well, I think a big thing with the the game on Sunday, it's like an early season litmus test for Aaron Glenn and his coaches and this program where they're at because the big discourse this week has been is it the Titans being awful and that's why the Jets looked as good as they did or is this maybe the start of them building on it and I I I think a major step forward. Obviously, you want to win, but this should be a game given the Packers injuries, how they looked in week one, the crowd, I think the fans, even with the rain in the weather, and we'll talk about how that impacts each team in a moment here. This should be a a game that the Jets have a chance to win. I'm not saying they're going to win. We'll save the picks at the end. But if you're truly taking a step forward as a program, your home opener against a team that comes in with some struggles up front without two of their best players, including maybe the best defensive player in the NFL, I expect the Jets to be in the game in the fourth quarter with a chance to win if they're truly building on what we watched in Tennessee altogether last week. I think the one thing you can take away from Tennessee that's real and not fool's gold is the way they ran the football and control the line of scrimmage because that's a pretty pretty good Tennessee defensive line with Jeffrey Simmons and those guys and and the Jets controlled the point of attack and I even I talked to Joe Tipman about it during the week. Frank Reich had a great comment yesterday, you know, he said, "Yeah," he goes, "It was kind of conservative play calling in the first half." He goes, "But we were running the ball so well, and when you get a chance to take a team's heart and soul away, you know, you capitalize on that opportunity." And that's what they did, especially, you know, with that 19play drive, uh, which ended with a field goal. They wanted a touchdown obviously, but they take the field goal. And that you could just feel, and Joe Tipman was describing this, how he's just, you could just feel the other side just wearing down and wearing down. And I thought it was an interesting wrinkle in their run scheme. You saw the guards pulling more than I saw last year. A lot of trapping and pulling. Joe Tipman said he loves getting out there on the edge when he gets a chance to block a DB. And Parm did it as well. And so I think more gap running schemes uh creates more of that physical mentality. Well, and think about this too, guys. I mean the I I love like Tennessee's preparation for this game compared to the Packers, right? So Tennessee obviously knew Jets have a pretty good old line. They're going to look to run the ball, set up some play action for Gino, whatever. Like there were some basic things that they had to obviously prepare for. They did not really have to prepare for three or four tight ends and Kenyan Sadi hitting 20 mph from three from three yards out, the Packers now do. So the more the more stuff that's on tape, well, now you can kind of counter that and go to other stuff that is not yet on tape. So I I know the rain and and the weather is going to be an issue. Although I do think that's an advantage for the Jets. We could expand on that in a minute. I I I just think that, you know, they're they look a little more whole and a little more unpredictable and a little bit more diversified, which obviously you have to account for if you're the other team. And, you know, the more time you spend in practice on X, well, maybe the more times Y is available downfield or a different aspect of the run game. So what they put on tape, even that block by Meoot, I forget who it was against where he just he first of all he just he slammed them, shoved them to the ground, hovered over them. He tried to get up, he smashed them back down and like the Nick the the Jets looked nasty. They didn't just look good, they looked dirty up front with those boys. So I loved it. Now you look at this Jets defense, Rich, and they're going to have to try and win this one without Ma Fitzpatrick. And I think that injury to me could loom large, not just this week, but the next couple of weeks given the offenses and the quarterbacks they're about to face. Your thoughts on what the Jet strategy is going to be in that secondary without Minka? Because I can promise you this, even with the weather, Jordan Love is going to be able to throw better downfield than Cam Ward did in week one. >> Yeah, well, that's a given. And I think this Minka injury is getting underplayed. Uh he's he's the the leader of their secondary. He's a guy who gets people lined up back there. He plays a couple of different spots. He plays in the deep half. He can play close to the line of scrimmage. He can even play in the slot. So, they're going to miss that versatility. You know, Dane Beltton can do some of that stuff. I don't think he can do it on the level that Micah Fitzpatrick does. And and you mentioned it, Jake. I mean, Jordan Love is going to throw it. I mean, I don't care if it's a monsoon out there. They are going to throw the football. He had 387 yards last week. They will go vertical. They will attack downfield. He's got Christian Watson, one of the best vertical deep threats in the league. Watson, I'm looking at my notes here. Um, he had 131 yards on vertical passes last week. They were four for five when thrown to him deep. That's going to be a huge challenge for the Jets secondary. The guy that I would be concerned about is Tucker Craft, the tight end. That'll be an interesting matchup. You know, I guess Belton would be on Craft. I I'm not sure how they would play that, but this is a huge challenge for the secondary. would have been a huge challenge even if they were all healthy, but now their leader is out and so that's that's a tough one. >> Yeah, it's definitely a tough one for sure. Not optimal, but silver lining, you know, if if you have your your brothers, I mean, would you rather see your leader go down in the first quarter basically first series and have a chance for 95% of the rest of the game to react and adjust without Minka, which is what the Jets had in terms of communication and guys getting more snaps than than they probably would have gotten if Fitzpatrick was playing for sure. So, you know, it it's not like it was just like out of nowhere and okay, now what do we do? Like they they granted it's a big step up from Cam Ward to to Green Bay's quarterback clearly, but you know, as good as Jordan Love is, I I don't look at I know he could throw it, but to me, he's not he's not a top five quarterback, not top six. He's he's probably that next cut for me. And I know he's going to try to throw it. That sounds good, and he's going to let it fly, but it I mean, it's it's going to be wet. So if they want to throw a 35 to 38 time, be my guest. And that obviously comes down to now, can the Jets control the line of scrimmage, even if not to the extent that they did against Tennessee running the ball. But the more you run the ball, you know, the less Jordan Love is going to be on the field with a chance to exploit some some holes back there. So that's important as well. >> I did some quick research before we came on. Jordan Love in in rain, uh he hasn't played a lot of games in the rain. uh a couple that jumped out to me where he had some costly interceptions in a couple of those rain games and uh one of them I think was a pick six. So FYI, I mean it's not going to be cold and rainy. We know that it's going to be a warm rain and sometimes that gets overblown. I don't know if it'll be windy. I don't think it's going to be windy, but it'll be wet. And I do agree with BT. I think it probably favors the Jets. The Jets want to make this an ugly game. Make it an ugly game. Make it a smashmouth game. Make it be played in the trenches. That's where the Jets have the distinct advantage. If the game is played on the perimeter, then it goes edgeto Packers. The Jets got to make it a phone booth fight and slugging it out in the trenches. And that that favors the Jets. >> Make the Packers feel the pressure. They've lost six straight games. They've had double- digit leads in four of those six. Like they if it's close in the fourth, let them be the team to make the mistakes and melt down. If you can get them to swim in the deep waters, they could drown. And they've shown you that under the floor these last six games. >> Yeah, that's true. That's a good point, Jake. And I was going to ask either one of you guys, you know, take whomever wants to take it. But, you know, playing in a foam booth there, that that sounds good. Um, but if you don't have the horses to do it, that's another thing the Jets do. So, I know each week it's it's a different matchup with different strengths and different weaknesses and inj injuries will really start creeping up for their oppositions. Jets as well. It's a long season. Already have a couple. But it's not like they're trying to enter this game and and do something that is beyond their personnel. I I think that most games that the Jets come out for, they're going to be able if not dominate, but at at least kind of control the line of scrimmage if they remain healthy. So that's an inherent advantage. They're not going to try to do something that they're not either ready to do or or have the horses to do. So, I feel good about that. >> Rich, let me ask you this because Aaron Glenn obviously is going to see three teams that he coached against with the Lions, including the Lions next week. Do the Jets have some sort of advantage they feel internally because of Glenn's connections to the Jets next three opponents? Because again, we talked at the top how it's a big lipmus test for the coaching. You would think Aaron Glenn going up against Jordan Love and Lafleur, there should be some something the Jets can gain from that matchup. >> Yeah. Well, Aaron Glenn was asked that question today and he he did say that, you know, knowing love so well does work in their advantage. Now, of course, there's always, you know, wrinkles and they change the scheme from year to year, but definitely having that background against Love helps. Um, the way I looked at uh so he's played he had four games against Love as a Detroit defensive coordinator. Detroit went three and one in those games and um they held the Packers under 20 point they held him to 20 29 14 and 31 and uh they had four takeaways in those games. Love put up some numbers you know he went over 400 in one of those games which Detroit won. But uh I think the having that background having the built-in scouting report in his mind probably helped with Aaron Glenn's game preparation this week. Same for Brian Duke or the defensive coordinator. He was in Detroit. He's familiar with Blub. So, it it's definitely a help to the Jets. >> I don't agree with that. Respectfully, Rich, I'll tell you why. I I think it's not that there's nothing there. I I hear you. I mean, it's there's both sides of the coin here. Now, you know, listen, it's I think it probably comes down to, okay, it's a bit of a chess match. But now Glenn's got to counteract that and and try to fool him, try to trick him. So, even if there is a bit of an advantage knowing, you know, playing against Love for those four games, I think it's basically offset because the other teams have the same advantage in terms of what Glenn does against them all those years in Detroit. Well, and and you know, uh, Glenn doesn't have Aiden Hutchinson rushing the quarterback or Brian Branch in the secondary, you know, Kirby Joseph like he had in those games against. So, I get it. I do think it helps a little bit. It's not going to be the deciding factor in the game, but I probably helped him a little bit in terms of getting a game plan together this week. >> The weather, we've alluded to it. Rich, you were the first I saw to tweet out the the towel for the white out that the Jets are doing for this one. Rich, are you expecting a big time crowd from the Jet fan following the week one win last week against the Titans? >> Oh, definitely. I I mean, if you can't I know the the rain is not ideal, but if you can't get excited for this, I mean, if you're a Jet fan, I mean, it's the home opener, your team's one and0, you got a shot to win this game, you you definitely got to show up. Um, yeah. I mean, I I I don't think a real fan would let the rain dissuade them from going. It'll be interest. You know, the Packers travel really well. I mean, we know that the Cheese Heads are are in abundance. So, I'm really curious to see how many Packer fans are there. Had this been a late season game, probably a lot more. I'm I'm really curious to see the distribution this week. >> Well, I got to say this too, Rich. I know you've dealt with this, Jake, from a from a writing perspective. I've certainly dealt with this over the years. Jake, I know you do as well. Like, we get this a lot like, oh, you know, and varying degrees, not not all-encompassing, but oh, you guys are so negative about the Jets. You always say this. You always I'm talking about all of us, not not anybody in particular on the panel. Yo, it's not our responsibility to conjure up false optimism. It's the onus is on the Jets to give their fans something to respond to and to react to favorably. And that happened last week. And that's one of the things you go back to some of the earlier shows like after the draft and over the summer. That's one of the things that I kept saying like, all right, it's it's not going to become Hinesfield, whatever the hell they call it now, or Lambo overnight. I I I get that. I understood, but it can't be a place where it's just sterile and benign and apathetic. So, the Jets finally embrace their level of responsibility. And I have no freaking doubt that the Jet fans are going to walk into that stadium, hopped up. It's not a cold rain. I can tell you the players, it was a definite talking point in the locker room this week about the players anticipating the home reception, especially the way it was in Tennessee. So I can And he also said, "We'd love it if they're really loud. we're on defense, you know, so the crowd noise could be coming back during the game. Um, I know the Garrett Wilson was talking about it, you know, he said basically we haven't given them a lot to cheer for in recent years. You know, now is a chance to to try to get a good trend going, you know, forward here, try to create some sort of home field advantage. So, I know from being in the locker room that it is it is a definite the players are are really pumped to see it, see, and feel the fan base. It was really cool to see Deario Bree, you mentioned it, Garrett, even Aaron Glenn, I think we played it Monday night, opening his presser, thanking all the fans who showed up in Nashville. And I'm with you, BT. I know for a fact the Jet fan is on fire. They are desperate. They want to see this team get the 2 and 0. And the energy is going to be there. title: Nick Sirianni on Win vs Tennessee Titans
text: Any questions for the coach? >> How you How you feeling after a game like that? >> Yeah, um shoot. You know, there's going to be a lot of things we need to correct, but obviously um great way to win. Um you don't get you only get so many of wins like that. And uh just good resolve by the team and good uh you know um I think it was a good, you know, just a organizational win, just being able to like everything mattered in that game with the with the heat and the way we handled everything. Um And you don't do one of those things or one department's not quite where they need to be or whatever, even just just one thing. If the attention to detail by the entire organization was was uh was outstanding. Yeah, you know, we felt like that obviously was the best uh move for us. Drew's naturally a center. Um and he can do both. Um but we felt like that's his best natural position. Cam's played guard. It's been a couple years, but it you know, he's played guard and he played he's played both at a high level. Um And that's just the way we decided to go because of those things and we felt like that was our best lineup that that gave us our best chance to win uh this game. So, um that's kind of some of the things that went into it. >> Do you think it will be that way going forward? >> We'll see. >> I know you guys wrap uh sideline catches quite a bit. You got a bunch of them today with Quentin and Darius in the right play at the game. Um how do you think those guys were taking to that coaching? >> Yeah, I think everybody here is um you know, awesome to coach. Um you know, our job as coaches is to get them better fundamentally so they can take next steps of their game. And obviously also, you know, that's the major job of the position coaches. That's I feel like that's the major job for me as the head coach. Um and then, you know, also the coordinators and the coordinators' job are to put the guys in positions to succeed. And our guys, I think we've built trust with them over the years that, you know, all the reps matter, all the all the reps and film matter as far as when we watch sideline catches. It's just great when fundamentals play out um of you work so hard at fundamentals and and sometimes those don't ever come up. There was a catch that I I think back on when I was in college, there was a catch that my dad used to make me drill that I'm like, "Dad, this catch ain't ever coming up." He's like, "Well, you're going to do it." And and that's when I was in high school when we were making those ca- the the and it didn't come up till my junior year of college. Like this type of baseball turn catch. And I'm like, "Man, that that guy just knew. My dad just knew." Um and sometimes they don't come up and sometimes situations don't come up. Um but you work them anyway and you and you put yourself in those positions anyway um in the attempts of when they do happen, you know, they make a difference. They make a difference in those guys uh their you know, their elevation as players and make a difference in wins and losses. >> Next to calm, the the sense of calm that Jalen Hurts plays with, uh combined with kind of the way he he uh transfers his will to everybody, what what does that do for a team um in games like this? >> Yeah, you know, there's ups and downs in in every game and we talked a lot last week and and every week it's going to be important to be able to play the next play. And when your your ca- your quarterback and your captain on your football team is is doing those things, I mean, what a great you got no better you got no better example. We we love to look for examples of great overcoming adversity or playing clutch in moments or playing through pain or whatever it may be. And then the best examples that you have are when you're doing it as a football team and then we'll point that out and and we'll we'll talk about that. There were so many things I felt like I wanted to talk about after the game that I didn't even get to that and that is a huge deal, you know, Jeffery Simmons comes through make a big play forces an interception. I got a ton of respect for him. He got he's a hell of a football player and then, you know, he's able to he's able to flush it. Jalen's able to flush it and lead us down the field in a in a critical situation and yes, got a just proud of the way he played and the way he had his resolve and that's but that's who he is, right? I that doesn't surprise me. He he's that on a daily basis. He's he's, you know, constantly in the moment and it's just a great example of your habits take over in these in these moments, right? You can't expect to be somebody different if you haven't practiced that the entire time and that's who Jalen is. >> Nick, you guys after all of the combine, you know, Saquon going out, Dallas going out, how were you guys able to do that >> We got we got great guys backing them up, right? Landon going out, right? We got great guys going that are backing them up. Credit to Howie and and his staff of the talent we've gotten got here and a credit to our coaches of the developing that talent and with their fundamentals and putting them in positions. Um and so that's why this is the ultimate team game, right? It it's it's the ultimate team game that takes everybody and it's such a good I you know, it's such a good example of what happened this week of all the preparation that went into it. Um So I love football. That's why I think that's why the country loves football, right? And that's their best sport there is and that's sure as heck why I love it. >> Nick, it looked like you had to get an IV after the game. What details can you share about what it was like? >> Yeah, it was. >> [laughter] >> And uh >> What was it like managing that game? >> Yeah, I didn't play a snap but I was hot. So, um you know, um yeah, the guys battled and and they again they just dug deep and I give credit to the Titans. They dug deep, too. And that's why if anything was off in our preparation, it wouldn't have given us the best chance to win, but it just took everybody and it was hot and everybody was hot. You know, and uh you know, and it took all hands on deck and you know like I said, I didn't play a snap and I had to get an IV. So, I just I just so appreciate how much the guys prepared. I so appreciate how much they fought through cuz it wasn't easy. It's not It's not easy and they fought and they clawed and they scratched and did anything they had to do to to to to get the win. >> How did you go for the win in that How did you go for the win in that overtime at the end? >> Um just that drive down the field was a big big-time drive. Um you know, they take they take the lead there and and then just we had to go we had to go down and and you know, you're playing the game you're you're seeing how the drive goes. Our men's mindset was, "Hey, I took those timeouts before the 2-minute warning so we could go down and have a chance to win." Now as the game goes as that drive goes, you'll figure out how that's going you know, our foot's on the gas. Aggressive aggressive aggressive. As you can always pull your foot off the gas. If you get there, there's not a lot of time left and you know, and say, "Okay, I can play this one for overtime." but you can't restart it. You know what I'm saying? Like you can't go, "Hey, I'm going to play this for overtime." and then and then put your foot on the gas late. It just doesn't work. You just don't give yourself But we got down there so fast and we scored late, right? And the touchdown, you know, with not with what 9 seconds left to go in the game. Um, but it was a tribute to the explosive plays that we hit down the field. And so, our mindset going into that was, "Hey, let's go minimum tie this game, but our mindset is let's go win this game." And our guys made plays, Shawn made great calls, Jaylen made great throws, Smitty, Tay, right, made some phenomenal plays. The protection was really good. Um, I'll take a a tired O-line over a tired D-line all day because, you know, I felt like the protection on that last drive was outstanding. Um, so >> Nick, they said >> The Titans said they wanted to grind on the on the ground again. Um, do you grade it on a curve because of the changes up front and because you're still adjusting to the news? >> No, we have a standard that we want to play to. We'll look at the tape and see, you know, see what happened and uh, you know, we want to be able to to run it more efficiently. I haven't seen any of the numbers, but, you know, everything comes off of the run and the play action and and and so, um, the guys battled though. That's what you're so proud of there, but we're going to go back to work, right? I think I didn't even tell them. I think they have off tomorrow and then I'll maybe I'll make that announcement on the plane. They'll they'll be excited about that with the long week, but then they'll get back in, we'll go right back to work on Tuesday um and watch the team the tape and and try to get better from it, but there's there's room for there's definitely room for improvement as we all know. We all see that and uh but we're going to enjoy the heck out of this. >> The Titans said they wanted to say that the Titans said they wanted Jaylen quarterback. Uh, six years into this, how do you feel when you hear something >> You know what? You don't get wrapped up into any of that stuff. Um you don't get wrapped up in any of that stuff. I you know, it like like Nolan said, like we all have phones, we all can we all hear that. Like you guys my information, like I have a phone, but it doesn't really I don't have a lot going on on it, but my information comes from when you guys ask me these questions and Bob prepares me for these questions. You know what? I I think Zach then when you get so wrapped up into that, like if I were to get so like I love our guys, so of course my natural instinct is like, oh, I want to fight. But when you get wrapped into that, when you get wrapped into the battle of words or revenge or what whatever it is, anger, last about 2 minutes in a game. It does. At the end of the day, the fundamentals take over, the situational awareness takes over, you playing together as a team, your toughness takes over. Because that all wait that all fades. That all fades and it's like that's why it's so important that you lock into what you can control. I can't control what anybody else says. I can control what what I focus on our team on. Because my experience with that, I've played the other side. I've played the other side where I got so wrapped in that and I'm emotional, right? And it's like I've played that side and it it's such a minimal time where it last. At the end of the day, it comes back to the details, it comes back to the fundamentals and it comes back to you having a clean mind of not letting anything else dictate anything but your your best and and your work. >> How much How much How much will game experience with the offensive line weigh into how you make the configurations on board? >> Yeah, we'll see how that goes. You know, um you know, like our old line, like our depth and uh yeah, we'll we'll continue to try to do what's best for our football team. >> Last one, Kaden. >> Nick, you've described in the past De'Angelo Cooper being a dirty work guy. Actually, when you see that in a moment like that, what what does it mean to you? >> Oh, that's [clears throat] the best. Like I I I think back to one of my favorite guys, Zach Pascal. And I say one of my favorite guys cuz I got so many favorite guys. This has been a great team. And it was so great when he was been able to be rewarded. Like I think back in the 2022 Zach kept blocking our wide receiver screen against Pittsburgh. And we it was the weeks before. And then they're like, "Well, Pascal's in the slot and Goddard's there. There comes the wide receiver screen." And Goddard comes here, Zack Pascal over there. He slips up through the there and and gets a touchdown and explosive play because of the dirty work he's done. And Zack was a benefit of that a lot of times in India as well. I think J.J. Arcega-Whiteside, you know, was doing a lot of the dirty work in '21. And we would bring him in tight against New Orleans in a 4-minute situation where we really needed that we were up big in the game. New Orleans comes storming back. Now we're up, I don't remember, 33-22 maybe in the game and we're in a 4-minute drive and J.J.'s in that tight split. And he needs to looks like a it is going to be a run. He's going to do the dirty work and we run an RPO and bam, he gets it. He gets a big explosive play. It happened to him in the Giants game as well in '21. It's so It's so awesome when guys are rewarded for doing the dirty work because it takes everybody. And And sometimes it happens and and sometimes it doesn't. Um but I knew Darius Slayton would be ready to make a play when he needed to make a play. And he made a couple nice plays today and he did a lot of dirty work. And he made a big-time tackle on special teams and he's he's a guy that man, who plays his role. Um we're going to continue to need him to play his role and and excel at his role and and he's accepted his role and he's starring in his role at this particular time. Great teams have you know, good teams have guys that know their role and accept it. Great teams have guys that star in their role. And And Darius Slayton has done that. >> Mark, thank you.

I think situationally us being able to be sharper and put it all together. I think that's going to be uh key. >> How do you How do you stay so calm when the game's on the line? >> Just preparation, you know, great focus, and great poise throughout what's being done. Romelo Height, the rookie defensive end/outside linebacker, broke his hand, has to have surgery, but there is an outside shot that he does play this next week, probably with a club of some sort against Arizona. Same news on Mike Evans. He's okay. The 49ers will just have to manage him this week. And indeed, high ankle sprains for James Thompson Jr., the rookie defensive tackle, and for Demarcus Robinson, the veteran wide receiver. Timeline for Robinson, 3 to 6 weeks, three at the best, but probably going to be more than that. And Shannan said likely IR guy, but uh the 49ers have only eight return from IR designations and they already have a lot of players on the list. So he told me that they've got to be careful about who they put on IR. They're still deciding on Demarcus Robinson look at Buenavista Cafe where the Irish coffee was essentially invented. Hey guy. Hey, hell of a job everyone in here, man. Hey, I believe we have a really good team and that's what a good team should do. All right, guys. Hey D, I know they moved it on us, but we kept them out of the end zone all game till the very end there. All right, lots we can do better, but lots of good to be proud of. Oh, the first time in 40 years that a Niners team has scored on the first five possessions of touchdowns. a hell of a job, >> guys. I felt you guys from the beginning to then just like I did last week, man. Enjoy the night. You guys have earned it. >> MVP team win, boys. Love you guys. Early in the season, you guys know how it is. Let's watch the film. Be hard on ourselves. Got a high standard here. But everyone, man, complimentary football. That's how it is. That's what we do to teams. Here we go. NINERS ON THREE. 1 2 3. >> Let's move back to Brock Birdie. 99.7 QBR yesterday. That is the official number. Guess when Patrick Mahomes last put up a 99.7 QBR in a single game? Never. This was at the top of the week's list by a mile. And that includes the Josh Allen performance against that terrible Detroit Lions defense. Allen and Perie are the early MVP favorites. Brock yesterday on throws of more than 10 yards downfield was 10 of 10, a perfect 10 of 10, 211 yards, a touchdown, and a nearperfect 152.1 passer rating. To make things even more perfect, there was the symmetry. Found Kyle Yushek. Same play as the first career touchdown against the Dolphins. Annie met Dan Marino before this game and Dan Marino wears number 13. Brock Perie ended up at 13 yards per attempt. The reason that Brock Purie wears number 13 is because of Dan Marino. That was Shawn Pery's favorite quarterback and ended up being Brock Pur's hero growing up. Exact 13.0 yards per attempt. exactly 13 yards per attempt after meeting Marino before the game. On a teamwide basis, this is the first time in history that the 49ers have started a season with back-to- back 20 plus point victories. And Brock Perie is now fewer than 100 pass attempts away from being the all-time NFL leader in passer rating. On top of that, there have been 2,439 qualifying games, games in which EPA per play has been measured for quarterbacks. Brock Pury owns two of the top four out of those 2,439 games. He also has the most games in NFL history over his first five seasons with a quarterback passer rating of over 140. That not to be confused with QBR. QBR is a better stat than quarterback rating. It's it's more specific, but Perie is obviously excelling at both of them. One thing that I will say about Brock Perie is that the improvement has been very nuanced for him. It's had to be nuanced because he was great from the very start against the Dolphins back in 2022. That's why I love the symmetry of the pass to Kyle Yuschek. It was the same play, the same hop over the end zone for Kyle Yuschek. We could see how well Perie defeated the Blitz against Miami as a fresh rookie in 22 and how well he's doing it now as a veteran for the 49ers in 2026. So, when we measure Brock Bird's improvement, then we have to look at it from a very detailed granular level. and he really talked about it after the game on Sunday. >> I went back and just watched a film with Mick Lombardi and where I was at last year and it's like if I'm hanging on a guy in a progression, it's like how can I find an outlet and uh or a checkdown and and stay ahead of the chains and and ahead of the downs and it's okay to be in third and medium rather than forcing a ball and being third and long and um stuff like that. So obviously, yeah, we we know our looks when we have opportunities to make big plays, but um playing quarterback is dishing it out and staying ahead of the chains and taking completions when the defense has given it to you. So um I feel like I've had to learn sort of the hard way throughout my career so far on some experiences and some scars, but um I feel like you got to learn and and make improvements and make change. That's that's what I did this offseason, I feel like. So hopefully I can keep that up. You have to give a lot of credit to the 49ers coaching infrastructure around that quarterback position because to take Brock Perie who was excellent to begin with and turn him into arguably the best quarterback in the league, it has required a serious attention to detail. You heard him talking about Mick Lombardi, the quarterback's coach. Klay Kubak this off season was talking about keeping Brock Perie in the pocket. And remember Klay used to be the assistant quarterback's coach to Brian Greasy who was Pertie's first QB coach. and now Clay is the offensive coordinator and obviously you have Kyle Shanahan on top of this whole brain trust but the weaknesses I thought early on for Brock and obviously they were very very minute they were very small but I would say that we talked about it a lot the the first year in 2022 if you would flush him to his left which is normal for a right-handed quarterback because it's unnatural to spin around and throw but flushing him to his left led to poor efficiency flushing Brock Birdie to his left no longer leads It's the poor efficiency. You saw it with the uh play the off schedule play to Mike Evans early in the football game where Mike got both of his toes down. And the other weakness might have revolved around Brock Birdie bailing the pocket a little too early in some situations. We didn't see him step up into the pocket all too much. And that one might have even persisted into last season yesterday. And against the Rams, Brock Birdie has manipulated the pocket so much more deafly. He is seeing over the middle of the field. He always has been good at attacking the middle of the field. It's like he's primed Russell Wilson without Russell Wilson's biggest weakness. But in order to exploit that as often as possible, you have to step up successfully in the pocket. And Klay Kubak emphasized that this offseason. Mick Lombardi emphasized that this off season. And the results speak for themselves. This is the first time in 49ers franchise history that they have not allowed a sack over the first two games of the season. And a lot of that obviously is credit to an offensive line that has jelled. I think people underestimated the need for health there and they underestimated the power of having five guys who have played together in the past. But Brock Perie is the hardest quarterback to sack in the NFL. And sacks are more of a quarterback stat than anything. Data has proven that time and time again. Perie led the league in pressure to sack ratio last season. Obviously leads the league in pressure to sack ratio this season since he hasn't been sacked a single time. That remains the case despite the fact that he has stepped up in the pocket more which goes back to his physical traits and obviously the coordination and and cerebral mastery of the game. He is feeling the pocket for the 49ers and he's got that insanely fast 10 yard split and he's able to put everything together to move in absolutely elite fashion. So it has put him again in the upper right of this analysis. And look who else is in the upper right. Jackson Dart is going to be playing against the Rams tonight. That's what is on tap. Rams against the Giants Monday Night Football. Rams, there's a lot of pressure for them to win for a whole lot of different reasons. 49ers have successfully finished the Australia trek. I think yesterday could be considered part of that because there was always a danger that there'd be some negative carryover effects due to fatigue, jet lag. They were able to overcome anything that might have arisen. Didn't doesn't sound like it did based on talking to guys in the locker room. And now the Rams are in a spot where they do not want to be like this cable car. The Rams need to stop the downhill slide. That cable car is not stopping its downhill slide right now. Heading down to Aquatic Park. I don't know if should I get back in the water today, guys? The cough is subsiding a bit, but I want to make sure that I'm 100% for 49ers Cardinals next week. Couple more notes. After watching the tape yesterday, here are the 49ers pressure numbers. I told you Nick Bosa would have a healthy amount. He had five. No sacks because the 49ers probably still looking for a little bit more bookending pressure, but Osa Deazua second straight game with three pressures. Grayson Halton has been impressing. And these pressure lists get used to seeing names like Fred Warner and Maris Seagull on them. Raheem Morris even blitzed Fred Warner off the edge. We're going to see more and more of that, especially against mobile quarterbacks. The 49ers, if they can't get that bookending edge presence for Bosa consistently, might have to blitz in order to generate some of what they need. But Maris Seagull was really good. He had that hard hit on special teams. Uh, I thought Jier Brown actually played a solid game for the 49ers as well. There might have been one missed tackle that uh gave up some leaky yardage from Jier Brown, but but he is doing a good job crashing into the back field. Led the team with 12 tackles. And I think that they tightened up the screws on the run defense in the second half. 4.3 yards per carry in the first half for the Dolphins when they controlled the football. Only 2.6 in the second half. But still something that the 49ers would like to fix in closer games because it's harder to gain leverage against the run game when you don't have a lead. And as good as Brock Perie and company has been offensively, you can't count on them to perpetually be perfect because then it wouldn't be special anymore. But yesterday, essentially perfect for the 49ers. One more Grayson Halton stat before we get to Kyle Shanahan. Pressure rate of 21.4% for the rookie. 7% higher than Osa de Gazua. 49ers have an interior pass rush again. And Halton is also stopping the run. This is this is a big big development for the 49ers. I've said it many times. The 49ers assumed he'd be a good pass rusher. That's why they drafted him. But there was a thought that maybe he'd be only a pass rusher because he's a little bit lighter. Called him baby Donald. Aaron Donald very light. But if he's stopping the run as well. So 49ers might have something cooking. Consider that as we listen in to Kyle Shanahan's conference call, guys. Um injuries from the game. Mike Evans had a hip. Uh we'll have to manage him this week. Um Romelo Height uh he broke his hand. He's going to have surgery tomorrow. um uh outside chance to be ready um for the game Sunday. Um but he needs to get surgery on that tomorrow. Um Demarcus Robinson has a high ankle. Um James Thompson has a high ankle and um and that's it. Go ahead. Kyle, do you have a timeline at all for Demarcus Robinson? >> Um, I mean, anytime it's a high ankle, you know, that's we don't have a timeline, but just high ankles in general are anywhere from three weeks at the best, which is very rare, to six weeks. So, you know, we'll see how it goes, but most likely it'll be an IR candidate here. Uh, is there a plan to have some wide receiver tryyouts or are you uh looking towards getting Jordan Watkins, um, Jacob Cowing involved? >> Uh, no. I mean, we expect those guys to be up and everyone's got to get more involved. Um, but, um, I know our guys, John and his group are working on all possibilities, looking at um, everything that's out there and, um, our options here for this weekend going forward. Is is Cado Hajj also a guy that you can see being involved in the offense a little bit more as opposed to just special teams? >> Uh yes. I mean know he's he's been out there the last couple weeks. You know, he had a catch yesterday um later in the game and he's been in on on some um he got he made some key blocks versus the Rams. So pretty much all our guys who are up we we always mix them in on offense, but as you lose starters and stuff, those guys um have to be able to do more and more. Kyle, are you at a spot right now? I know that that pup and and IR list, you have a limit as to how many you can bring back. So, are you at a spot where you're having to balance, you know, not automatically placing somebody like Demarcus on IR to potentially preserve one of those returns? >> Uh, yes, definitely. I mean, that's those guys are right in that area with him and James of how long those take, but um we're trying to just we got a lot of guys. It's real early for us to have as many people as we've had. So, we got to balance all that out. So, we're not we're not settled on our decision yet on who will go to IR and who won't. >> Kyle, with with Mike Evans's situation, um, and you managing him, you managed them a lot since camp, but it seems like he and Brock have kind of that instant chemistry, or there simply two guys, uh, playing at the top of their ability. >> Um, I mean, they Mike's done a lot of work here in the last couple weeks. you know, he's been able to practice each day um since since going down to Australia um and last week. Um but no, I also think I mean they're two really good players, so usually when you have two really good players who are both instinctive guys, um it's pretty they they gel together pretty fast. Kyle, how would you assess the performance of your defensive line? Um, yesterday it was a tough line. They couldn't get off the field that quickly. What did you see from this film? >> Um, I thought they did some good things. Um, you know, I mean, there there's certain plays we'd like to have back, but um, you know, getting the four sacks, I thought, you know, I definitely thought we could have had more, too. Um, I thought they did a really good job, but you know, we had big goals of not letting that quarterback scramble. um up in the pocket like through the B gap and things like that. So, I thought they caged him really well in the pass rush and made him escape backwards um which was our goal. Um there's a couple run plays I'd like to do us a little bit better on where we got out of a gap and a lot of big one, but um you know, especially losing uh a D lineman in that game too where we had some five down fronts and only having having three interior guys for the rest of the game. Um but those guys overcame some big challenges in that game too. Did you get any more information about whether Mike will be be able to resume practicing this week? >> Yeah, we're going to hold till next week on that. You know, if we were if we let him go, he was just going to do individual this week. So, just don't feel the um riskreward of letting him go this week when he's just doing individual. We're going to try to hold him so we can hopefully replicate that on the side and get them going for practice um hopefully next week. is the same with Christian Kirk. >> Um he's not an option this week. He's not there yet. So, um we got to wait another week on him at least. >> Kyle, what have you seen from your young defensive lineman at Grayson Halton, Romelo Height? I know Romelo Height's going to be out but uh potentially with surgery, but what did you see from those guys? Um, I mean, I think that they I think they both did some good things in week one and I think they both took a step forward in week two. Um, I thought Grayson flashed a lot. I thought Romelo had a much better game, too. Um, really running his ass off all over the field and I thought both of them took a step in the right direction. >> Uh, how good did Brock Card's film p uh pan out? >> Uh, it was real good. Um, it's, you know, he was almost flawless. His his last play was probably his only miss. um unintentional grounding. Um I thought he was pretty perfect. He he had a unbelievable game. >> Uh Kyle, what have you seen from your safeties and Marquis Seagull and Jerger Brown? Um I know Malik was a guy who you got wanted to start last year. Where is the the competition between those three? >> I think they've been doing great. It was just unfortunate for Malcol that he missed all of training camp and you know he didn't get healthy till we were down at down in Australia and those guys got a lot of work together and um really kind of has solidified that job um by how they played throughout the preseason. And I think it's shown here in these last two weeks. I think they've both played very well. Uh Malik did get in there for a few plays and I thought he played really well when he got in. He's been looking great in practice, too. And um getting right back to where he was. So, um we got a number of guy, we got three guys right there who could all start for us. So, um it's a good problem to have. >> What did you see from your running game when you looked at the tape? >> Um I thought we had a chance for a couple bigger ones. You know, it's we got that one holding call called back. You know, I don't think we ever really I never really got the run game going as as far as a play caller. I mean, just only having 20 plays in the first half, only having two drives, um, made that very hard. Um, the only time we really stuck with the run was the last two drives in four minute and we were just trying to run out the clock. So, um, I really got a chance to get it going and and then also the way they played us, they blitzed us so much that we felt there'd be a lot more holes in the passing game. Um, and it kind of worked out for us that way. look like he was uh like he was a lot more explosive this week as opposed to last week. >> Uh no, I thought there was no difference. I mean, it's just easier to see his explosiveness when he gets in space like that. And you know, we got him down the middle on a double corner blitz, you know, so they they don't have enough guys to guard everyone when that happens. Um so you get it you get him in space and his explosiveness will jump off the screen. um didn't have that opportunity for the Rams. >> Kyle to two games in, have you been happy with the coverage units on both kick and just kind of larger picture? I know it's the second year uh with with Brand where that progress. How do you look at that from point A to point B from the start of last season? >> Um well, I mean, I was real happy with how we played last year and I think we've done a real good job in these last two weeks, too. I mean, I thought we were unbelievable versus the Rams. Um you know, Arizona definitely did. I mean, not sorry, not Arizona. Miami did better against us um yesterday. Um but but I still thought overall that we um played a real good game on special teams and on our kickoff coverage. >> You you kind of alluded to it by bringing up Arizona. So, I'm just wondering, have you moved on and started just the uh checking out what what Lafur is doing down there and uh kind of anticipating get the game plan going tonight in the next couple days? >> Yeah, that's um that's actually that's why I made that slip up there. What's on my mind right now is um soon as I'm done with you guys, I get to move on to Arizona. So, it's um got lunch here and um then then we'll start. >> Well, what do you Well, what do you think of them so far, Kyle? What have you noticed? anything off the bat or what you've heard about them? >> Uh, no. I mean, I I haven't turned on their tape yet. That's why I mean I'll do that as soon as I'm done with lunch after I'm done with you guys. But, um, and I I know how well they played in week one. And, you know, I know the score wasn't um wasn't close yesterday, but I was told that they played them a lot better than the score. I heard it was tight um um going into the second half and they just pulled away, but I haven't seen any of it with my own eyes, so excited to get started with it. I expect it to be good. They they got a lot of good players. Michael Flair does a I know how good of a coach he is. Their defense has been together for a very long time. Um I know how good of a job their D coordinator does, how long they've been playing together. And I mean it's they're a team in offseason. We expect it to be good this year. Um, I'm expecting to see that when we turn on tape.

title: News on MIKE EVANS and more from the 49ers locker room…
text: I just stepped out of the 49ers locker room after that blowout over Miami here at Levis's and the first big piece of intel. Mike Evans is okay. Indeed, a precautionary exit due to the hip issue, but he would have been in there if the 49ers hadn't been ahead 35-6 or 35-13. Point number two, and we'll get to a couple of these injuries later, but I talked to Trent Williams in that locker room, and I think he's got the best summary quote on Brock Pury. >> Like I said, we starting to witness the um Brock's prime, and I think um it's going to be it's going to be a a whole a sight to behold. >> We are just now climbing into Pert's prime. He's 26 years old. what he did today up until that last intentional grounding and I'll maintain that Cal Shanahan should have taken him out and put in M. Jones, but until that last intentional grounding where the 49ers wanted a hold or a pass interference, Perie had delivered the only perfect 100 expected QBR game in NFL history. And I think Fred Warner has a great point. >> Unbelievable. you know, and you know, I've spoken on how how great of a preseason he had and his camp, his command of the offense, but it's different, right? I mean, we get judged on those three hours that were out there. And so, um, for him to be operating the um the offense the way he is right now, it doesn't matter who who the other pieces are, right? As long as Brock's the one that's being the point guard, I mean, I know we're good. >> This is Tom Brady like stuff. Back when Tom was at his best, it wouldn't matter who was playing receiver for the New England Patriots on a year-by-year basis, he would find a way to make it done. Now, he never put together a 100 QBR game like Brock Perie did or, you know, it counts like he did today. It was I thought at that point in the game, you go to your backup and then we would have been talking about actual history. Now, speaking of perfect 100s, Christian McCaffrey did deliver his today. So, Brock's QBR once ESPN releases the the final number after all these games is probably going to be 98 or somewhere around there. It's not QB rating, it's QBR. It accounts for the 30 rushing yards and and for the fact that his only incompletion outside of the intentional grounding was a drop by Debo Samuel. So, it was pristine today. But Christian McAffrey scored his 100th career touchdown. 50 with the Carolina Panthers, 50 with the 49ers. A perfect split. And Christian after the game, this these were his thoughts on his quarterback. >> Yeah, I mean, he's he's special. Um I I think that'd be the the word I I'd use for it. I think when him and Kyle get on a roll like that, it's so fun to watch. um you know, as as a running back, obviously, you know, you want to you want to roll, but when we're running keepers like that and they're putting six up and kind of selling out, it's why, you know, you can just see the the keepers open up. I don't know what he I don't feel like he threw an incomp completion the whole day. I don't know what the stats are, but um it's unbelievable to watch that and and to how decisive he is, um how good he is at throwing on time and then also creating when he has to. Uh, you know, when he's at the helm, we feel good. >> Let us take an extended look here at the field at Levi Stadium before the sun sets here on this Sunday night up in one of the suites. It was the home opener here at Levis's. A little cameo by E40 ahead of the Dolphins. Purely accidental walk there in front of the tunnel. That was cool though. And then we saw Kyle Yushchek and George KD do a press conference in tandem. Thought this was really neat. Both of those guys taking the lect turn as the two longest tenur 49ers. They're the two guys who have been here since 2017 when Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch took over. So Yuschek's been on the team a little bit longer since he was a free agent who signed in March and KD was a fifth round draft pick in late April or early May. Anyway, those two players now have lockers next to each other. Yuschek actually moved his locker this year across the room to be near KD and McAffrey. Did the press conference together and I think they had some great points about the 49ers offense. First off, I want to say pretty sure the Niners are undefeated every time me and Juice both score touchdowns. >> So, let's keep doing that. Um, great record. And then Mike Evans is good at football. >> Uh, he's helped our offense out tremendously. Um, and it's good, too. It's like our offense line has basically been the same. So, like they've been able to met uh like kind of gel together. Um, Brock's confidence has continued to skyrocket and the receiver room is a little weird. You know, obviously we just keep getting guys are getting banged up, but um you know, Mike Evans is doing a great job. Drock is doing great when he was out there. And you know, Debo's finding his stride, too. So, I mean, and also you have Chris McAffrey, too. So, our offense is just really fun right now. And I think Kyle's just feeling himself. >> I was going to say, and George summarized it pretty well. I think what he's saying is that we have a lot of weapons on this team. And I it's that's not particularly like new. I feel like that's been the case for many years here. Um, but it's a lot of weapons that have now had the time to gel together. Um, that continue to grow. Brock gets more experience. The offensive line plays together longer. And I just feel like we we still get to excel and continue to get better and better. Now, >> the 49ers had to be on their game today offensively because you've got to give the Dolphins a lot of credit for how they were able to play this and expose some of the 49ers weaknesses on run defense. >> Yeah, we let a few of those drives go a lot longer than we had hoped and that's definitely probably the number one get better is is stopping the run a little better. Miami somehow held the 49ers to just two possessions in the first half. They had 85 rushing yards in the first half, 19 minutes of possession. And you know, I said that this was going to be a dog fight just because I respect Jeff Halfley. He learned from the 49ers. He's applying some of or a lot of what Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch brought to the table all those years ago. And a 49ers game plan, especially back in the era when they were underdogs, would be to suck the air out of the game. And the Dolphins were able to do that in the first half. Except that Brock Perie said, "Well, you might have the perfect game plan, but even if you give me two possessions, I'm going to make sure that I lead touchdown drives on both of those possessions." >> For me, it was like, dude, we had two drives in the first half. You know, they were eating up clock and stuff. So for me, every play, every drive mattered. Um it wasn't like we went out there and just blew these guys out. Like it was a it was a game. And so I mean that that's what we're saying. Like that's the NFL. So that's where my head space was at is like how can I protect the ball? How can I move the ball, take be in the right looks and and be aggressive um and keep us ahead of the chains. So that's where my mindset was at really. >> And I mean we saw so many insane plays today. The Py to Mike Evans connection obviously elite. first when Perie was off schedule in the first half and then in the second half it was so fascinating because uh it was one of those plays where if the throw is any worse it's probably an interception to Mike Evans but the pump fake that Pertie did to spring it open Evans obviously wasn't the first read on the play the DB was trying to undercut that football but just an absolute dime as Kyle Shanahan said from Brock Perie, plus all those runs, 30 yards of rushing set up the Miami Dolphins. He was on one today. I've talked about the game against Arizona back in 2023. That was the only game that was statistically comparable to the one today. Unbelievable stuff. Now, Perie, though, has grown over the course of his time in this league. He was very good at the start, but he talked a little bit about the growth that he made with the QB coach Mick Lombardi this off season. >> I went back and just watched the film with Mick Lombardi and where I was at last year. And it's like if I'm hanging on a guy and a progression, it's like how can I find an outlet and uh or a checkdown and and stay ahead of the chains and and ahead of the downs and it's okay to be in third and medium rather than forcing a ball and being third and long and um stuff like that. So obviously, yeah, we we know our looks when we have opportunities to make big plays, but um playing quarterback is dishing it out and staying ahead of the chains and taking completions when the defense has given it to you. So um I feel like I've had to learn sort of the hard way throughout my career so far on some experiences and some scars, but um I feel like you got to learn and and make improvements and make change. That's that's what I did this offseason, I feel like. So hopefully I can keep that up. Now, obviously a big issue for the 49ers is receiver health. Demarcus Robinson, high ankle sprain. He's probably going to be out for a period of time. They are now down Ricky Piol. They're now down Dejon Stribbling. They're now down Demarcus Robinson. They had to put in Jacob Cowing and Cadrell Hodgej into this game. I think as long as you have Evans, you feel with the level that Pertie's playing at, you feel decently good. But what happens when you start playing some of these better defenses? I don't know about the Cardinals next week, but the Denver Broncos come here to Levis's in week four, and then it's the Seattle Seahawks on the road in week five. Now, potentially salvaging news here is that Christian Kirk is going to be eligible to come off of injured reserve in week five, and they're going to need everything they can get. And we could look further down the road and we can look at the fact that the 49ers should get Dejon Stribbling back what they think around week 11, week 12 of this season. Obviously Ricky Pierce saw out for San Francisco for the rest of this season, but and and you've got to stay afloat with Mike Evans as well. Good thing is that George KD looks like he's getting that explosiveness back following the Achilles. And again, when Perie is playing like this, then you can get away with a whole lot of injuries. Defensive side of the ball, the rookie defensive tackle, James Thompson Jr., probably a high ankle sprain. Kyle Shanahan said the 49ers had already been in contact with Leonard Floyd after Sam Okuanu went down. That was right when they were leaving to Australia. Obviously, no signing there, but Shanahan said that signing is going to have to happen at some spot along the defensive line and at wide receiver because those are the two spots where injuries have been piling up for the 49ers. Now, obviously that that run defense is something that I think the 49ers were able to successfully bury over the past two weeks because of how good the offense has been and the secondaries obviously played really well for San Francisco. But Fred Warner explains the dynamic here. >> I wasn't super happy about it, but at the same time, you know, I think it's it's continuing to get better, right? we're we're starting to continue to uh feel more confident about, you know, where where everybody's fitting and getting on and off blocks, getting the push that we that we need and we want. So, um I I I have to I have to watch the film. It's so it's so hard like in this moment to kind of figure out exactly how how it all fit up. But, um you know, you mentioned it like the fact that our offense is scoring like they are and forcing teams to pass the football, that's in our favor. We will see what the personnel moves of the 49ers are as things are a little belleaguered up front, but I mean they today I mean the number for the Dolphins was 4.3 per carry in the first half and down to 2.6 in the second. Pandya says that many of these injuries probably including Shivers can respond to rehab even if they are fairly severe. At least, that's what the world thought. That's not what Tyler thought.  Shook. So, shout out to Tyler Shook, the Ravens. That's a Ravens shake-up. It's a...it's a big win, man. It's a big win. A big road win. I mean, we already talked about them, but what about the Bengals? I think it was another big win. Why? Because they're showing they're a consistent team now.
