title: Dak Prescott & HC Schottenheimer reflect on bounce-back win, Cowboys' all-time passing TD record
text: Uh before I get started, I just want to uh say uh to Jaden Daniels, what a great competitor, man. And uh I know he'll make a a great recovery, but uh what a great player and uh you hate to see that in our game. >> Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News. Your thoughts on your offense today. Looked like they were scoring almost every other possession it seemed. >> Yeah, you know, we were disappointing ourselves last game. I was disappointed myself last game as a play caller. Um had a great week of prep. Felt good about the plan and um you know we we did a nice job moving the ball and we the plan was to come out and throw it around a little bit. That was the plan. I know the run numbers were pretty ugly. Um but uh that was a little bit of the plan coming into this game. >> Sidi and Dak just were just a pretty good connection today. [clears throat] >> They spent a lot of time together, man. They've thrown a lot of balls together and um you know it was uh really great to see Dak break the record at home. Uh two CD uh I thought you know George made some really tough catches at at really big times for us. Ryan Florenoi Fergie couple touchdowns. Um I just thought you know the passing game was hitting on all cylinders today. L deal us Cowboys. Uh you see Dak locked in. Obviously came in with the with the Roger jersey and and you know he's he's sent messages, you know, going to training back with the Cowboys Super Bowl jersey and come in with the Rogers jersey. Was he locked in more tonight? >> No, he's always locked in. You know, um [snorts] you know, I thought the focus on the sidelines throughout the course of the game, you saw the competitive fire in him. I mean, the guy's just a different unique competitor, man. The way he's wired and the way he loves his teammates, he loves this game. uh he loves the Lord. He talked about that. You know, his confidence comes from his faith and uh you know, just couldn't be more proud of him. But uh back to your question, you know, he and Cid have have played a lot of football together and it was really cool to see those two guys connect. >> You weren't here at the beginning, but for a fourth round pick to come in and and end up at the all-time league record holder of all the passing records in Cowboys. Just let's say about Dak and his career so far. I mean, the man, you know, you can't talk about Dak, the player, without starting with the man. The man is unique, you know. Um, he's just special. That's why, you know, I was emotional watching the guys celebrate him in the locker room. I hope the cameras caught it because you could see the love and admiration that he has from all of his teammates. I mean, they literally, the way he plays this game, the way he leads us is uh special. He's a unique special special man. and I'm blessed to to be able to coach him. >> Brian Todd Archer with ESPN. Can you kind of take us in the locker room there? You usually make the announcements of what happened in the game. Did you save Dak for last? >> I did. I did. Uh yeah, we started with uh field goals, then we went to defense, then we did the touchdown passes, and then we went to Daks. And on uh the fourth one uh we had the ball and uh we uh presented him the ball and uh he was able to make a amazing speech to his teammates and as you guys can imagine it was a lot about um what motivates him and it's not about him it's about them the guys looking at him um and uh it's a very emotional scene. Is there any probably not knowing your personality, but is there any part of you that came into this thinking needed to win this one because you don't want to go to Brazil 0 and2? >> No, I I you know, I was um like I said, very excited to get out there and compete again. We know we're a better football team than the one that showed up in New York uh last Sunday. And uh I think we showed that tonight. And um again, a lot to clean up. There's some things still on third down we got to clean up. I thought we did a really nice job defensively in the red zone. I thought that was great to see that. That's that's big. You know, the the fourth down stop at the end of the half was huge. And uh I just thought we played better, but um you know, we were we were excited about this opportunity. >> John Mashoto with the Athletic uh after you guys I think your second touchdown cameras caught you on the sideline. Obviously, you're really emotional uh and excited about that, but then also when you guys got the stop right before halftime, looked like you threw your headset a little bit like you just seemed very emotional about it. Why do you think that you were so emotional in the first half of this game? >> You know, I think it was more of again just, you know, I know what we have, you know, and this is this is a tough business. I know what we're built from. I know what we're about as a group of young men that have come together and forged a special and unique brotherhood. and they have a bond and um you know I hurt for them last game you know and you know because we didn't play our best football but I knew what we were capable of and um now we got to go and try to stack some wins >> and I know you got to watch the tape and still talk to Christian and that but from your sense did you think the communication was better on defense? >> Yeah, I think it was. I I think you didn't see the I mean they got us on a double pass that you know uh fortunately they couldn't connect on that but uh overall I thought the communication was better. Uh there's certainly things to clean up. We certainly did a poor job of containing Jaden, you know, but he can do that. He he does that to a lot of people. That's really where the rush yards got away. And then, you know, we got we got some things to improve on third down. I thought we really rushed the passer well. I don't know what the pressure numbers were. You guys will have to give me those. I know we didn't get any sacks, but he was he and Marcus were both, you know, moved off the spot quite a bit. And so, um, I felt good about that. But there's always things to clean up. You know, we certainly have not arrived. [clears throat] We, uh, we got a lot of work to do. >> Ask Cowboys. I know you said the plan coming in was to throw the ball a little bit, but 66 yards rushing. What do you feel like initially? I know you have to watch it back, but wasn't working for you there? Yeah, you know, again, I I didn't think the numbers would be 66 yards, Tommy, but like I said, I did want to come out and spread them out and, you know, use some of our play action passing game. Um, you know, Dak did a really nice job running. And then again, we had the long one called back in the fourth quarter. You know, that was a nice run uh by Javvante and, you know, it's a it's a good front, you know, and they're they're they're explosive and powerful and they they uh they did a nice job. But again, the commitment there from me was, hey, we're going to come out throwing the ball around. And I think it worked pretty well for us. >> And then Jan Barhan today, I know that you don't want to put too much into the green dot role, but for a rookie to handle that, how do you feel like >> Yeah, I think he did a a really tremendous job. You know, we had to rotate green dot some when Shamar would come in in certain packages, I thought overall we handled that really well. And then, you know, Jan, you know, had a couple stingers and uh he's tough, man. And I think you love that about him. We knew that's what we were getting when we drafted him and uh he showed that tonight. M the fourstar telegram. You mentioned Jaden Daniels injury there at the top. What do you think his exit did to this game overall? >> Um you know I don't know hypothetically for them you know I don't know. Um you know he's just an elite player. He's elite player. I've heard he's a great person and I just hate to see it. >> In terms of your defense, you know statistically it looked like it was a little bit better but you think you guys made enough of an improvement from week one to week two? >> Uh until I watch the film I won't really comment on that. I don't, again, we don't feel like we have a finished product. Um, I think there's a lot of things to clean up. Like I said, the third down, we got to get people off the field on third down, but the red zone was an improvement. We won the turnover margin, which is good. That gives you a chance to win. Um, but, uh, like I said, the one thing I'll say about the defense and, you know, CP this week was they were like this, man. They didn't they didn't blink. You know, I've been in a tough situation like that before as a young coordinator and not sure and you taking a lot of bullets. uh he didn't he didn't he didn't blink and that's a sign of a competitor that uh has a very very bright future. >> In terms of your offensive line, you had a pretty significant >> exit with Tyler leaving before the start of the season. How do you think you guys perform that kind of departure? >> Yeah, you know, for the most part, I think it's been really good. You kept TJ Bass. That's why we tendered him how we did. Uh we really, you know, cherish his athleticism and flexibility and versatility. And uh I thought all in all they played really really well protecting the passer and um you know the the makeup of that group is one of toughness and grit and uh I love watching them play. >> Yeah. Tim [clears throat] Kalashaw Dallas. This is kind of like Clarence's question but you've watched a lot of football. You're pretty old. [laughter] >> Damn. Tim, how old are you? >> See you're not near as old as me. >> Okay, good. Got a chance. Good. >> Nobody in this room is I don't think. >> Maybe Ed. >> Not Ed. Sorry. [laughter] Sorry. Sorry. Sorry. >> Nikki. Nikki's it. That's the end of [laughter] the road. Um, for him to be breaking all these regular season records, not a franchise that had Romo, Aman, Stallback, Danny White, Meredith, all those guys, most of them played about 10 or 11 years like Dax in his 11th year. What does that kind of say about him, too? >> You know what? I I've been I've been blessed, Tim. I've been around some elite elite quarterbacks. Um, and Dak Prescott's preparation is something that is abnormal. They all work. They all prepare. They all study film. But this guy takes it to a different level. I mean, just the amount of film he watches, the communication, you know, he's up in our office till all hours of the night, you know, and watching, you know, film, you know, with with a couple of our coaches. And um it's just unique, you know, and I think that's what that's what it takes and that's what you love about the guy, but most people don't see it. The fans don't see it. I mean, he's there till 9:30, 10 o'clock at night. You sometimes I feel like I got to kick him out, you know, but uh special young man and uh he deserves everything he gets because he does it for his teammates and his brothers, not himself. Elwin Henderson Mirror. Brian, how tough is it going to be to have a normal week of practice with this long Rio trip coming in to keep things as close to normal as possible? >> Yeah, players will be off tomorrow. It's going to be it's going to be unusual. Um, Tuesday is Wednesday and then we'll finish the game plan. So, we're going to treat it like a short week and uh then we'll fly uh Thursday night through the night. Get down there, move around a little bit Friday, but uh it's you know, we're used to weird schedules and and short weeks. And um you know, got beat up a little bit, you know, tonight. You know, I mean PJ Lock's got a foot. Um Kobe Durant's got a hamstring. Got to get some more tests there. Bar him had a stinger. He came back, but we did get beat up a little bit. So, we'll figure that stuff out in the morning. But um yeah, it's a unique week, but one that we're looking forward to and we'll take any test people want to throw at us. >> Bless you. >> Excuse me. >> Ed worker, WFAA, still trying to overcome uh your shot. >> Yes, I apologize. I really do. >> Was there any thought in your mind that you wanted Dak to set the record tonight at home rather than in Brazil? No, you know, I just I I as we were going through that last drive, I I could tell they were playing a little bit tighter on the outside, so we saw some things from a matchup standpoint. Um, but uh the hardest part for us was, you know, we called that play a little closer than we usually do. And in true Dak fashion, he he was fine with it. I kind of asked, "Are you good with this?" He's like, "Just nod." And then the catch seemed like it was incredible. Like it could have gone either way. And Cidd Sidi wrestled away. since we can talk about Brazil now that the Washington is over. Uh a lot of talk >> I don't really have to talk too much about Brazil. >> Well, >> are you going to Brazil? >> Yes. >> Okay. >> With you. Um so much talk about the fields. I don't know if you have you had any meetings about the fields over there, you know, the playing fields. Were you guys on that part? >> Yeah. Again, you know, we talked a little bit today um you know, with the operations people. Todd Williams, his team have been in direct contact with the league. the league seems to feel like everything's going to be fine and uh in reality, you know, we were focused on this, but you know, I'm I I have no concerns if >> the soccer team saying that the fields are >> I'm aware of some of their quotes and stuff, but again, I trust that the league is going to make the right decision and they'll get the field up to standard and uh but like I said, Todd Williams and and his team operationally were talking to the league office and they were working through that in through last night and into today. So, >> you lose two guys in the opener at safety and linebacker and then today you lose at least another safety and you mentioned Barham. Does it kind of go like that at positions a little bit? >> Yeah, usually the positions that hit your strongest and you end up getting injuries and you know and Maris Bell I thought did a really good job stepping in there. You know, he's obviously um one of the leaders of the special teams group and I thought he was you know inserted in there and did some really good things. But um we did carry the the two practice squad elevations for Baron and Robinson. That was a big part of special teams and that certainly helped us out at linebacker. >> Your kicker makes another 60 yarder and no one bats an eye. Do do you ever get used to that? >> Um I never I never hesitate to throw him out there. Actually, I really if it's anywhere near midfield, I just send them. I just point. I'm like, "Yeah, field goal." That's all I do. I just point. Oh, sorry. Uh, Caleb, like you broke up a pass there of a hearthead. Just your thoughts on the surface of what you saw for him tonight. >> Um, you know, I think again I don't want to speak out of turn because I haven't seen the film. That was a great play. Um, you know, this guy's growing as a football player. He's growing as a leader. Um, I saw him come over in the third quarter. He had a really good question that he asked, you know, Christian Parker about. um something schematically that he wanted to make sure that we were right with. Um so the curiosity I think is great, but uh yeah, terrific football player. I thought Malachi Lawrence showed up today. I felt like he had some really good pass rushes. Donovan has a rocku. Um like I said, I wish we could have finished a few of those, but man, they were moving those guys off the spot and they're both pretty athletic guys. Uh about a little bit after what Todd Todd asked what Todd asked rather >> you have a guy make a 65 on the 70 yard field goaling [snorts] now for a while. >> Does that completely change the way you call a game? >> Yeah, I don't take it for granted. I'm always trying to get a little closer. Uh but you know, I'd be lying if I didn't say Dak and I, you know, we do talk quite a bit about like no negative yards. if you're somewhere around midfield. We feel pretty comfortable that if we don't have a negative play that we're going to have a chance to get points and um he uh is a tremendous tremendous weapon. And the thing I love about him, man, is like most of them it just like you can't see it. You guys see it better, people see it better on the TV copy, but like I'm never worried because it's usually right directly down the middle of the goalpost and that's unusual. >> Uh coach, can you talk about the impact of Kamad Turban? Yeah, I thought he had a couple really good returns tonight. Um, you know, still want to get TP going a little bit on the offensive side of the ball. Um, you know, we, uh, try to get him involved on a little toss, crack play to the edge. Uh, but, uh, as a returner, he's been close and we feel like we're ready to pop one and, uh, maybe it's going to be in Rio. >> And special teams, when will we see Aubrey from 70? >> Um, we're not afraid of it. So, you know, stay tuned. Could be could be anytime soon. >> All right. >> Thanks, guys. >> [laughter] >> See with your >> head on. >> We had the same reaction. [laughter] >> Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News. Uh, your thoughts about surpassing Romo as becoming a franchise leader in touchdown passes. >> Uh, I'm blessed, honored. Um, as I've told you earlier in the week, right, records are meant to be broken. This is my time to break this one. Pretty cool. Um, to do it against, you know, the team I scored, I threw my first touchdown against what, 10 years ago or so. So, um, definitely humbling. Um, something I don't take for granted the the great history of this this organization of the past quarterbacks before me, obviously wearing to me the greatest one, right? Um, and so, uh, super super honored, super thankful. God's great. Um, I'm not taking it lightly, but as I told y'all, it's just the beginning. I want to double it. I plan to play for a while. So, just getting started. >> What' you think of your teammates and the way they honored you in the locker room afterwards? >> Yeah, that was um made me emotional. Uh, I mean, I love those guys. I I I lay it on the line each and every day. My love for this game, my love for my teammates. Um, any and every teammate that I've had. you know, there's tons of guys that aren't in that locker room that that I think about when I break this record, whether it's them them catching the ball or them blocking um or them on defense, you know, and just giving me confidence and getting the ball back. And so, um but to see my teammates act that way, to see guys that only have been together for, you know, five, six months, you know, um have the joy, have the cheers that they do, uh it it was emotional. Um very, very appreciative of it. Shows me what this brotherhood means. Um, it shows, it reminds me that everything that I do, uh, the conversations that I have don't go unnoticed and, um, just reminds me how blessed I am. >> Clarence Hill, DLS Cowboys, why did you choose the word Roger today? >> Yeah, I mean, we're just we we're talking about it throughout the week. Uh, yeah, he's just on my mind and, uh, yeah, home opener. Um, knew that this was an opportunity to break this record. Uh, and just felt right. Just felt right. As I said, I mean, he's the he's the standard. He was the the first great great great one here, right? And I think it still is. And as as we you know, I was schooling up Q on the history of him, you know, to uh win the Heisman, to go surf our country, and then to come back, win two Super Bowls, be the man that he is, um be as great as he is off the field, do so much for the community. Um he he's the epitome of what a Dallas Cowboys quarterback should be, and he's he's who I'm chasing. And so, um, thankful for the relationship that we do have and, um, yeah, just wanted to to support him. >> Do you allow yourself to even look back to 2016 and envision one day I'm going to own every passing record by a Cowboy quarterback in franchise history? >> You're asking if I ever thought that? >> Just think about, you know, can you allow yourself to see where you were then and see where you are now in this? >> Yeah. Excuse me. Uh, yeah. Yeah, I mean I mean you know when I threw it on the side when I threw it and got to the sideline and all the guys you know were coming up to me even then some of those you know memories and flashback like I said flashback to the first you know touchdown he throwing against these guys 10 years ago some of those you know memories highlight reels or whatever you want to call it rolled in your head um and it yeah it's a reminder but I don't do it often um for for one yeah it makes me emotional um knowing everything that I've been through everything that it it took to even get into the NFL and you know the doubters whatever it may be and just the constant belief in yourself and shows me how great God is and when you believe in yourself and you're founded and you've got strong faith what what can happen but um as I said this is just this is just a step this is something that you know back then at 23 years old I was pretty confident then and and maybe even a little bit more arrogant I would say than I am today and so I would have told you then if you really you know asked me that I was going to do this and I don't think that I would be here if I didn't think that way back then. And then I heard the crowd. I'm like, did he catch it? Did he not? And you know, when he's running down uh the end zone, I'm like, thank God. Yeah, this is over. We can just move on and just play ball now. And so definitely fitting. Um that guy he he's been he's been amazing and as I just said, we're just getting started. He's just getting started and so uh he he's a hell of a player. We started off these first two games with two touchdowns and um right or one he's had one touchdown in each game and I don't think it's going to stop. Uh just his mindset, his mentality, just where he is in life. Um it's only going to get better and I'm excited for it. >> Then the guy who caught you first was in the locker room. >> Yeah. to does that make you think back to it that you know there's Dez with Dez's kid and didn't think about >> Yeah. It just creates uh for great chemistry. Super thankful for, you know, who Dez was or who he is and, you know, the the older veteran he was when I came into the locker room, you know. um first first guy that ever greeted me walking into the locker room, one of the biggest supporters of young guys. Um gave me so much confidence and then now to you know be pouring that into CD and you know CD you know tells me right after the game run on the field nobody's more deserving um I'm just super blessed for having those guys but it's not just on the field it's off the field and and that personal relationship. >> Now to go to Brazil I mean did you ever think like okay you can't go 0 and2 and go to Brazil. [clears throat] >> Yeah, definitely was think we can't go into going going to Brazil and definitely wanted to get this out of the way in front of our fans and I mean look forward to going to Brazil but you know I'm sure more of our fans are here and so I wanted to get it done, get it over with and I think it would have just been odd doing it out there in Brazil and so um it was a great day overall. I mean both teams we've played half right and so that gives you know CD the opportunity for some one-on- ones and he's going to keep doing what he's he's done in these games if they're going to do that. Uh can you just talk about y'all's relationship and why the relationships from your teammates make up this record just as much as the off performance? >> Yeah, they make up more than the than the records. Um this world's about people, man. This this life's about people. And yeah, me and Jake obviously have grown close over this off seasonason and just over the past years. And then, yeah, when he lost his father in camp, that was a I knew where he was. What was working so well to find that again for two scores tonight? >> Uh, yeah. That's stuff that, you know, we talked about that that's actually almost identical to a play we talked about last week where I wanted to hit him and I didn't think he gave me his eyes fast enough. And, you know, we had a conversation on the bus about it and, um, wasn't the exact same play, but we came back in a very, very similar look, very similar attack, and he did exactly what I wanted him to do, and I just trusted it and ripped it, and he made the catch. And um that that's what those conversations and all those you know moments on the bus and all that those things matter cuz you never know when they're going to come up and came right back up tonight. >> And then you talked about playing here and how special that is 610 and one here over the last two seasons. How important is it to get a win like tonight [clears throat] and stack them here where you guys were winning a bunch in 22 and 23 and have that advantage? >> Yeah, you just said it's trying to create an advantage. Um, and you know, if you could do it at home, that's that's half or more than half of your games that you know, you're you're giving yourself a good chance to win that and then you go get some more on the road and you put yourself in a great position to make the playoffs and great momentum uh going into the postseason. So, um, it's just that's NFL football. You've got to find a way to create any advantage anyway that you can. And if you can make your home field advantage real, uh, we've got to do that. And so, it's always great playing care. I do and I seriously mean it. I just challenge our fans, you know, to to really take pride in that as well. you know, third down or just anytime our team's on on defense to to take pride and like they mean something here. Like when when when we're on defense, like their energy, their noise, their passion for the game, that helps our defense, that helps get the other team off the ball, may create penalties, may create uh, you know, false starts and all that type of stuff. And, you know, it puts pressure. I know you go we go into other weight crowds and um, it's not easy to communicate. And so I just challenge our our fans to to take pride into that and and to step it up a little bit and you know not wait for the the players to amp them up and understand that they have a play a part in this. Edward, WFAA, what awareness is there among your teammates and coaches when you're about to set a franchise record uh for touchdown passes? And does that lead to receivers campaigning to break the be the one who receives the record ball? And is there any conversation about this is for the record, don't throw at the stands? >> No, it's it's one of those things you don't talk about. Uh I'm guessing because it wasn't talked about, you know. Um, I don't care to talk about it for one. So, I think people understand that and they're not going to mention it to me, but I don't think there was even side conversations about it. Um, maybe that was why I was probably a little frustrated, you know, in a couple of drafts all stalling out because I just wanted to get it over with. Um, and just going in the game plan, I laughed. Uh, you know, we we talked kind of about that on the sideline and some guys knew it, some guys didn't. So, to answer your question, and some coaches knew it and some coaches didn't know it was about to happen. And, uh, I know Shotti knew, you know, it was an opportunity. I know he wanted to get it done and I mentioned that on the sidelines like yeah when I saw some of these red zone plays and um builds I was like oh yeah Shotti's a good guy he wants to he wants to give me a touchdown he wants to get some touchdowns and find some easy ones for me and so uh yeah it wasn't talked about much >> Tim Kalashaw Dallas Morning News I believe you were two years old last time Cowboys won the Super Bowl so I know your knowledge of Troy and especially Roger is pretty much >> film based video >> but uh but Romo always breaking records here when you were at Mississippi State. What do you remember about your awareness of him as a quarterback then and then when you came in and ended up with his job? >> It's interesting you said it like that. Um, uh, yeah, I was a big fan of Romo. Um, I was I was a fan of the Cowboys and so, you know, led into being a fan of the quarterback of the Cowboys, you know, as frustrated at times, you know, as he was or as some fans are of me. And there was a tweet out there, right, that when I got drafted that was brought back up and you know, I was just a dumb fan at that time, too. And so, um, yeah, I didn't know exactly what he was dealing with, you know what I mean? So, uh, but I do remember watching him throwing it to Dez, throwing it to Jason, and I the the accuracy, the command. Um, those are the two things that that that I I was in awe, you know, and then you get, like you said, I get drafted here and I remember sitting in meetings listening to him and Scott talk and they were talking so far over my head. I'm like, man, this is going to be tough to get on the field. Like, I had no idea what they were talking about. They're talking about building plays and formations and um yeah, [clears throat] and just his knowledge for this game. Obviously, that's that's evident just who he is. And even, you know, him calling games on broadcast, you can tell that. And so, uh that that that's what stands out to me, his command, being able to call his own offense, and then just ultimately the accuracy, being able to make any throw and every throw from whatever position he's in is something that I've always admired and looked up to. And um yeah, thankful for for the relationship that you know, me and Tony have. Tony was always always has been great to me. Um you know, even even that year with with whatever and everything that went down, um he was a great supporter. He was there to help me on the sideline, you know, all the way throughout the year and when we've been able to connect in the offseasons or I've asked a favor or vice versa. Um it's it's been mutual. So um super thankful for him. >> Mac U Mac in the football start telegram. You mentioned you're a rookie year. If someone had told you that when you got picked, you're going to go on and do all this stuff, records, contracts, fame, endorsement deals, and all these records, do you think you would have even believed it that you would go on and do all this stuff with one this franchise? >> Yeah. Um, absolutely. And that's credit to my mom. That's credit to my brothers. Uh, you know, I' I'd said I would do some of these things when I was a a little kid. You know, not being naive is is great. You know, Jerry said that on one of the openers to to a Hard Knocks uh one of the Hard Knock episodes, and I thought it was it was amazing. You know, sometimes it's great being naive, and I was a little naive, you know, just growing up thinking that I could do this and I can do that, but yet I think it put such a uh insurmountable belief in my head that that I can accomplish whatever I want to accomplish. and any thought that I I said or any um thing that I wanted to do and I mentioned it and I said it out loud. I had a mom and I had brothers who who poured gas on those thoughts who who told me I could. And um as I said, you can call it arrogance, you can call it confidence, belief, whatever you need to. Um I wouldn't be here if I didn't have those thoughts, if I didn't believe in myself like that. And I just encourage, you know, the next little kid out there, you know, who comes from the trailer park in Louisiana or wherever he may come from and doesn't know if he can do it or have the resources or have the family that you're right, like believe in what you want to believe in and and find the people that that support that and and you can do it. Uh that that's what makes me so emotional. As I said, I want to double this number, but to be even be in this position is now being, you know, 33 years old and just thinking back of like why did I think like that, you know, and it's because of my mom. It's because of my brothers. It's because of the people I was surrounded by. Not just them, my friends, my teammates in in high school, middle school, whatever it may be. And um yeah, I I truly truly believe I wouldn't be here if I didn't have those thoughts. And so uh naive, arrogance, whatever you want to call it. Uh I'm thankful that I did and and they're not going to stop. >> Garrett Pel, CBS Sports, Dak, you're wearing Rogers jersey after decades. What do you hope people are thinking about you decades from now when you rewrite the record books like this? >> You know, I don't I really don't think about that. Um I don't um it's not that I don't care, but but for me it's about being present. You know, when I when I hear that that Jake, you know, pivots that that conversation there or I see the way that my teammates react in the locker room or when I score that touchdown, that's enough for me. like that's more than enough for me that, you know, when when I'm done playing this game or when I'm not here anymore, life's life and life's going to continue to go on. Um people are going to look up history. People are going to believe what they want to believe. The simple fact that I actually had to explain Rogers history to a teammate, you know, uh there's going to be Cowboy players that don't give a damn or know who I am one day. And so, um I just want to be present as much as I can every second and every opportunity that I have. And I think that'll be enough. >> Sitting Dak, whenever the record happens, did you think of your mom? Like >> when when it happens, the catch is made, what are you thinking? What are you saying to her? >> Yeah. Um, I don't know. I woke up this morning just just a little emotional, way more than than than normal. And I don't know if it it had a part in God knew I was it was going to happen today and I was going to break this record and have to talk to you guys or not. And so, yeah, I don't know. Um, I just felt it. And you know, uh, actually the touchdown to Jake right before that play or broke that huddle. I felt like that was the touchdown to tie it. I literally in my head said, "Thank you, God." before I even snapped the ball. And it happened. And then on this drive, I was, you know, kind of like, "God, if you've got it in in store for me, let's break this thing and just get it over with." And, you know, the moment it happened, yeah, I just I just felt my mom. My mom was never short or never hesitant to tell me how proud she was of me. She was never never never short of that. And I could just hear that. And that's enough. Like thankful that my teammates, my my coaches, and everybody believe in me and all that, but but that's enough. And I heard that my whole life growing up and I hear it now as loud as I've ever heard it. And so I'm just blessed. >> Patrick. >> Hey D. Patrick Walker, Dallas cowboys.com. On Thursday, I brought to your attention Jan Barham's viral passion on did my research. >> Yep. So you saw it. I did. >> All right. So bringing it to present just as the leader on the team and one of the veterans in the locker room. What did what did it mean for you to see that young man second NFL game, first NFL starting to go out there and make the play he made to get you back the ball which you then got a touchdown off? >> Yeah, I wasn't surprised. Um he's a guy when I had a conversation when we first came in uh or when he first first got to training camp and it was a short conversation but when I walked off I'm like he's wired the right way for defense. I like that. And as I as you you know during our interview I was kind of lost. And then after that I went and watched the video. Uh and I think it was the next day or maybe two days after that that I actually you know caught up with him in the cold tank and I asked him like the media asked me you know I finally saw the video. Uh and it was just out of context to be honest with you. You know he was passionate. It wasn't an argument between him and CP by any means. And so um it it it it was the epitome of who he is. he wasn't happy with what they were doing and his performance and he was expressing that and CP was just saying we're going to be okay and so not surprised at all that he went out there and played this kind of game. I mean, just even how he answered that question to me and it's like, yeah, no big deal. You know, I just didn't like I thought we were playing soft or whatever and, you know, I was pissed off about it that yeah, I mean, he's going to be a great ball player for us, great ball player in this league and um yeah, he's just every opportunity that he gets the way that he's wired and what this game means to him, he's going to show it. And I think tonight was just his second opportunity in doing so. >> And I asked the same question to CD, I wanted to ask you, you guys got off to a fast start offensively. You also had a fast finish, kind of slowed a little bit in the middle. What's the key to keeping that that fast start and finish throughout four quarters? >> Yeah, just just it's it's one play at a time. And I echo and those guys know that, but you know, it's just human nature. You get up a couple touchdowns, you get a couple of store, a couple of scores, and you know, it may not be the whole group. It may not be, you know, everyone, but a player here, a player there just kind of lets off the gas a little bit, and it shows. This is a game where all 11 matters. Whatever's on the field, and I just think that was an example of that. And, you know, we we we talked as we do. We've got great leaders. We've got guys that take a lot of pride in their jobs and wasn't a lot of conversations or words need to be said and you know we got it back going and uh yeah that that don't let off the gas you know because sometimes when you do you put yourselves in a way much way tougher situation than you want to be in and in this NFL the ball bounces a funny way and now now now you're sick you know and so uh yeah just continue to play it one play at a time and and just trust the process. D Fred Davis 1053 the fan talking to the guys uh in the locker room after the game on the defensive side it was hey what was the difference because last week after the game shot said we need to be humble right and so these guys Vaughn Jaylen all said it was just a confidence thing really did nothing change in the preparation but it was a confidence thing you on the offensive side of the ball how do you go from you know we're not going back to what we did last year and did you notice a difference in just the confidence in this group this week >> the whole team of >> defense Yeah, absolutely. I noticed noticed the difference and um it it was in the way that we approached as as those guys mentioned in the way that we approached the process and how we attacked the week. We didn't change anything up, you know, we doubled down. And I think it was a question, you know, Ed asked me on Thursday of like why why do we have a a good record and being able to bounce back and it's because if you believe in your process in the way that you do, you just do everything just a little bit more and a little bit extra. And I know that that that's what they did on defense and we just did as a team. And I know that they were upset with themselves after last week because it was it was lack of communication. They gave up some big plays. They gave up some scores. And it was all things that were controllable and they can control. And so I think they went into this week preparing to to to do exactly that. You know, communicate as we we said there's two ends of communication, the guy giving and the guy, you know, receiving the information and making sure two both parts are clear. I think they did a a much better job at that tonight. And um but it's week two and I'm sure there's times that we've got to clean up. I know there there is on offense and I'm sure there is on their side but it's just great to to get this win at home and what I was saying earlier just the confidence builder and so I know it's huge for them just even after we you know broke it down um said that my little speech or whatever to the team and broke it down just to watch them celebrate for CP and I'm guessing it was CP you know it was water bottles thrown everywhere and somebody was in the middle so I'm guessing it was CP you know first win is a DC and so just to see that spirit that energy um confidence can grow from that >> yeah at Ron Murray K104. First off, big congratulations on the record. You know, you briefly mentioned, you know, just the journey getting to the NFL, you know, your name is going to be in the Ring of Honor. So, if you can go back and talk to a young Deck in 2016, what would you tell him? >> Just to keep going. Um that you're right. Um kind of what I was saying earlier, I don't think I'd be in this position if I didn't have those thoughts, the belief, and the confidence in myself then. Um so, it'd be a simple conversation of of keep going. Adversity is going to happen. Um it's inevitable. it had already happened at that at that age and so just understand when it happens you don't change your approach to responding to it and um that's what I tell myself again today Mike >> Mike Lesie WFA uh the Fox campers caught CD going hunting for the football afterward made sure that he got it back to you what does the football mean to you relative to the record and and the fact that he went looking so hard for it >> yeah it's awesome that he he went to go look for it just kind of goes in as I was saying you know the way that my teammates react was is humbling and it makes me as emotional as anything to see how much they care for it. Um, it'll be a good keepsake. Obviously, I've got it. I've got my jersey. It's not something, you know, I'm rushing to get framed or put up. I don't have a place for it yet. I mean, I'm not even my house. Yeah. So, it just collect dust until until my girls get old enough and they care to, you know, show somebody and show it off. But, uh, I've got the memories. I've got the relationships that that that that show what that football with the jersey means that um yeah, it's just a sign of it that yeah, it'll collect dust and it'll be a beautiful dust collector. >> All righty. Thank you, guys. >> Thank you.

title: Drew Lock and more react to Seahawks’ dominant victory over Cardinals | Postgame Press Conference
text: It's the family. >> Are you the same weight you were see or are you wearing heavier clothes in Green Bay? Like like it seems like you're lighter or or is my eyes just playing tricks on me? >> Uh it can play tricks a little bit. My weight's going up and down the same way. Okay. >> Good. >> Thank you. Thank you. Appreciate it. >> What up? >> All right. Does does it now after a few years of this feel like almost a script that your defense is going to keep you guys in games even when your offense doesn't start and it's going to end this way? >> I mean, I think that's something we've uh try to uh create in the defensive room uh from the start of Mike being here is like we always talk about being the tip of the spear and then even taking it further than that. the D line talks about being the tip of the spear of the defense and uh you know we really believe in the offense obviously uh they obviously got the job done had some great drives um but we feel like you know we want to win games with the defense. >> I think they only have a handful of first downs after their touchdown. What what did you guys do to really lock it down after they scored? >> I mean I think we did a great job of just like locking in the details uh at halftime. Um there was a few things where they were, you know, running the ball to the boundary, um you know, getting on the edge and things like that and uh we switched some things up and were able to stop it and uh you know, we stopped our offense. >> The way you guys just play so physically kind of on both sides of the ball seems like I mean today look you guys kind of just swore out physically. >> Yes, sir. >> I mean I think that's our identity. Um you know, you can hear coach Mike talk about it a lot is uh we want to be like a bow constrictor. That's how we want to win games. meaning like we slowly just uh you know defeat teams uh out physical teams and towards the end of the game they're just going to tap out and um you know I think we've done a great job of creating that identity and it shows up on tape. >> You guys have won 12 in a row now too. I don't know if that's something you think about that you guys have you spent you know 10 months since you guys lost a game. Do do you think about that and just kind of how how that >> I honestly haven't thought about it and I think that's what is so beautiful about this team. I don't think anyone's thinking about that. Um, I think we're so honed in on just being who we are. Um, you know, setting the standard, being the standard, um, continuing to grow, chasing edges, and all of those things that it's like we're never looking behind us at what we've accomplished. We're just always looking ahead. And, uh, you know, a lot of times we're not even looking ahead at other teams. We're just looking ahead of how can we become better. And, uh, I think that's why we, uh, have such an identity on tape. you know, if you're too busy out in the sideline getting ready for the next position, but do you ever get to just sit back and watch Jack's work and appreciate what he's doing out there? >> I mean, all the time. I mean, you know, we're sitting over there on the D line uh on the sideline and, you know, when he catches the ball, we're just like, man, this guy's a wizard. Um it's it's it's nice to have uh big playmakers on offense and, you know, we have long drives on offense. It allows the defense to rest. Um it's really complimentary football when you can uh be able to play like that. your sack, it looked like you basically like badge pressed the double team into the quarterback. Like how much satisfaction you take from winning in that way specifically? >> Uh, a lot because uh I I think I take pride in like allowing the edges to play off me as well. So I feel like even if I'm not getting the sack, that's something I do is I I burn the B gap. I try to take two guys with me to the quarterback and a lot of times that frees up the outside guy to to wrap around me and get the sack. Um, this time, you know, Dante wrapped around the quarterback felt the pressure from him and stepped right into me. So, uh, it goes, you know, vice versa sometimes. You know, sometimes I'm the sacrifice and sometimes they force the quarterback into me. So, that's rushing as one right there. >> Do you have a preference whether you like the three or the end? You play a lot at the end. >> Yeah, I definitely like the end. Um, I want to work at it a lot more. Um, I'm getting more comfortable out there. I feel like you have more opportunities to get one-on-one rushes and things like that. um avoid that center slide and things like that. Um but I'm definitely more comfortable um playing through technique. That's what I played my whole career and I I think I still prefer it. >> Anything else? >> One more. One more. Um so EJ last year had his comment in support of Sam. >> Sam said that really meant a lot to him and I don't think you guys lost a game since he made that comment. >> Do you then as a defense learn like hey let's pick up Drew the same way because we can see how how even us guys on defense can really impact the offense that way. Is that is that something you guys think about when you think about offense? >> I mean, yeah, for sure. Before this game, when he had to step up last game, that was something we already addressed at halftime. We were like, man, we got Drew's back. Uh, let's finish this game. Um, you know, let's make sure that we finish this game for Sam as well. And, uh, I think that's another picture of like what this team is about. Um, we're going to support the next man up. Um, and it's been done so many times throughout, you know, since Mike's being here is, uh, you know, one man goes down and the next man steps up. and um you know everyone is capable of holding it down. >> Thanks Leo. >> Thanks. >> We got the one touchdown and that's pretty much it the whole game. All punts and turnovers after that. Just what do you think about the way your defense performed? >> Um I think you know we came in at halftime made our adjustments. Um I thought uh you know we started playing sound ball um everything we needed to do you know fixing the little things. when the one turnover that you guys had on offense. How much pride do you guys take as defense and getting a quick stop after that and not letting it hurt you? >> Oh yeah. You know, we never waver. You know, it's his next play up. You know, we don't think about the play that happened before. We know that we have to go out there and execute. >> Leonard just told us that Mike's uh I think the word he used where he wants you guys to play defense like boa constrictor. What does that what does that mean to you? >> I don't know. [laughter] They be having all these words, man. Look, I just know that we need to go out there and play fast, physical football, you know, sound football. 12 is one. Um, we just need to be dominant in everything we do. >> How Mike mentioned they had to be on a silent count at the end of the game because the way how loud Seahawks fans work just how being a defensive team on the road and getting that kind of sharing. What is that like? >> Um, that's good. You know, our fans are the twelves travel well. You know, we love to hear that, man. It brings energy. It brings juice to our team. Just as a team, what what kind of confidence does it give you when Drew Law comes in and plays at the level he does? What's >> We already know what Drew can do, man. You know, it's a next man up mentality. We got full faith in Drew. Um we see him work every day and we go against him every day. You know, he faces us. So, you know, that's that's just, you know, we we when Drew was up, we never wavered. Um you know, we got full faith in him. We're back. How did that feel? >> Awesome. Felt really good. Um, yeah, it was it was a complete game, I'd say, from both sides of the ball, special teams as well. Um, our defense is is very good. Um, giving us the ball in some advantageous situations. And honestly, that first quarter playing out so weird. I think there was like five plays on offense. um you know them stopping them, us getting the ball, scoring quick, them having to go back out there, then us going three and nothing and then having to go back out there and just >> kept chugging away. Uh hats off to them for the way they played. Um talk about the O line for a sec. Holy cow. Um it's awesome playing behind those guys. They're an awesome group, an awesome unit. Picked me up all week. Talked through everything all week, man. They were so fun to work with. to be able to go on that drive that they did where all I had to do is say hut and hand it off to Eman who did a phenomenal job on that drive too. I was just awesome just awesome football by those guys >> to close to close a game out like that just like you said just handing the ball off pounding it just how satisfying is that as a team? >> Oh it's awesome. I feel I mean I feel like feel like it's something Mike um talks about often. We talk about pushing piles often. Um, finishing going forward, never backwards. Um, I I honestly feel like you could look at every play in that drive and say that we were trying to do all of those and probably succeeding almost. Now, pile pushes don't always happen, but they were going to try and I know they were. Um, awesome job. Even Jax on that play, the little screen to the right, making a guy miss, getting vertical and stretching for the first down to continue that drive was was huge. the first touchdown. How did you notice how quickly he shook that defender with the fake? How surprised were you all? >> I was a little surprised how I thought he was going to do it. Didn't didn't happen. Um but that's that's the like beauty of of playing with him. Um he's going to find ways to go. It might not be the most like conventional, but that's what makes him a ball player and that's what makes him one of the best receivers, offensive player of the year last year. Like that's just what he is, what he does, man. It's so fun to play with, which is why I think I probably could have gotten it out a step sooner, but sometimes you got to sometimes you got to see how it comes out. >> Was that supposed to be a go route the whole time or you shook him so much it became one? >> Uh, no. It was not a go route the whole time. >> Make it one stick and go. How did you think he was? You thought he was going to take longer on >> Yeah, I I never expect him to inside the inside release the corner. Um, that's just not it's just not a typical thing. But man, if he's gonna play you that far outside and you want to get vertical on him, go ahead. That was cool. >> Walk us through the other two touchdowns. I mean, this is a fun day for you. Let's go through touchdown number two uh to Jackson. >> Um, >> what what are you thinking at the line of scrimmage and then you snap the ball? Walk us through all that. >> Yeah, shoot. We We had the motion >> uh pushing a guy out wide to the right. They were showing me shell, which is like disappointing because like I wanted to go to the route that I ended up doing. >> Um, but man, I lift my leg. Both safeties kind of started creeping down. Ended up bringing zero on us with a couple poppers. And uh, you know, it's my job to get the ball out on zero obviously because we have just don't have enough to block. But when they pop, it then becomes my job to avoid the poppers. Jack's ring a fantastic >> over or through. [clears throat] try to go over um maybe to the side, but Jack's ran a great route and uh they ended up giving us the look that I was personally hoping for and and it worked >> When you have worked to get to this moment and you're thrown to the offense player of the year and you have this defense, all those circumstances, just like how much joy are you playing with? It look like you had a a fun time today. How much fun was this and and how does that compare to maybe some previous stops in your career? Yeah, today was a whole lot of fun. Um, I think it was just accumulation of, you know, obviously the work put in throughout the week. Um, everybody adjusting, myself, adjusting, coaches adjusting, the line adjusting to my cadence, receivers, the football. Um, it was just a fantastic job by everybody to move on like quickly and be ready for this week. Um, Coach Flurry and Coach Peace getting me ready for this game. Jay and Sam helping me out all week. It was just it was a lot of fun working with everybody in that building. It was I talk about how much I love the building and reason I come back. Like it it kind of just played out all week feeling love from everybody how skilled you know the skill guys are, how awesome the O line is up front. It's just a great group of guys and just going to keep playing good football. >> When you know at the start of the week that you're going to start, obviously you're getting the reps in practice that you didn't get last week, but is do you have to fight any sort of human nature to like overthink things and get in your head and put too much prep like knowing the whole week you're going to start. >> Yeah, I think I think you can definitely step out of like normal routines. Um, look for a couple extra things and um I definitely did that this week. You know, I watched a little more film, studied a little bit, looked at a couple things that maybe I wouldn't look at during the week, but I just felt like it was necessary. It was things that I needed a little clarity on. Um, and it was a lot of fun going through that process. It really was. I wouldn't say it was like a negative thing. Um, it's just mandatory things that you have to do when you're ready to step into the spot and try to go lead a team for four quarters. It's just it's necessary and uh, you know, it needed to be done. >> What were you thinking when uh, Rasheed fumbled the kickoff and then Chess picks it up? was kind of >> Yeah, it kind of was one of those like turn and walk the other way and then our sideline kind of gets excited. I'm like, "Oh my gosh, Jazz picked her up." Great field position. Um capitalized on it and it's a heck of a play by him. Former quarterback >> Drew guys who backups who have clearly starter traits like yourself, sometimes it takes a while to whether it's an emotional maturity or you learn something about the game, how to play the game, whatever. Now you're in in year eight. title: Aaron Rodgers & T.J. Watt Postgame Press Conference (Week 2 vs Patriots) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Aaron, what are you seeing some of the problems here? What are we doing with the offense, the rhythm trying to get going? What's going on? >> Yeah, I got to look at the film. Um but we just didn't get into a rhythm. We had too many three and outs again and um you know, just I don't feel like there was anybody that had an exceptional game out there. We all uh played below our standard. >> Talking with Mike, he's Mike was just in here and said that he felt consensus something was off on you during the same Thursday in practice. Is that something that you felt that things were kind of herky-jerky is the word he used? >> Uh yeah, I don't know. I didn't feel that way maybe Wednesday, Thursday. Um I felt like it was a grind. You know, we had a good grind practice on Thursday, but I'd have to think about that. Um >> What gives you confidence that this offense can and will have success? just what I've seen in practice, what I saw in training camp. You know, these are still the first couple weeks and you're going to see different looks and unscouted stuff and I just don't think we all adjusted very well to some of the stuff they were doing. >> How much did the last pressure >> Hm? >> How bothersome was the pressure? >> I mean, they only got me once, I think, but uh there was definitely um you know, the pocket wasn't as stable. But they brought a lot of six-man pressure. Go ahead. >> How much was the pressure? >> Yeah. >> Going back to what you were saying earlier, you get the idea that on third and long, you guys are going to pass the ball either drive back >> Yeah, it's frustrating for sure. We uh defense has been playing great, you know, they've been holding uh you know, [clears throat] 13 points a game in two games and offensively I think we're averaging like eight points a game, so it's not winning football. >> Aaron, in that drive before Jeremy's bobble, what did you see that that you like? Is Is there anything in that drive that you can you can use and build on? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, I love changing the tempo and I feel like you know, we had a couple uh couple good uh plays and some good motions. So, they played a little bit softer cuz they were up by 17, but um yeah, I like the rhythm of that. >> Aaron, what do you think you need to do to get more on the same page with DK, especially in the vertical passing game? >> Yeah, I'm not worried about it. You know, we're going to get it get it sorted out. We've been on the same page since uh since I came back. So, you know, I'll talk with DK like I always do and we'll be fine. >> Dylan and Zach both talked about what a leader you are. Dylan and Zach and Walker and they both talked about what a leader you are and like I'm sure today didn't go as well as you wanted it to. So, how do you encourage them when things maybe kind of kind of aren't going as well as they should be? >> Well, I think we got to take ownership as players. You know, we got to be accountable to each other about our performance. Uh mine wasn't good enough and uh you know, a lot of guys on offense wasn't good enough. So, we got to start with ourselves, not point the finger and not ride the roller coaster. It's a long season. They're you know, Super Bowl team from last year. We knew it was going to be a tough game. We had our chances. Our defense is playing excellent football. When they hold them to 13 points, we got to win the game. Um so, it's definitely on us to play better, but you're not going to see me panic. I don't think Mike's going to panic. Um urgency is going to go up a little bit, for sure, but no panic. >> You popped up pretty quick on that one where you did get hit in the back like that. Like how were you able to get up that quickly and didn't really seem like you were fazed? >> I've learned you got to get up quick, number one, so they don't try and send anybody out to get you. but yeah, that was definitely a shot, you know. I haven't taken too many of those in my career cuz usually I have a feeling you know, if we're picked up or not picked up. Um that was a uh lapse in communication obviously there. >> Aaron, how do you expect this team to react to an in- increased urgency? >> Well, I think you know, as long as the leadership steps up, uh can't feel sorry for ourselves, can't point fingers. We all got to play better, but I think we can all give a little more, you know? All the best teams are player-led teams, so we got to keep taking the ownership, and in a game like today where there wasn't a lot of flow to it, we need to be better, and it starts with me at like making sure Mike knows what's working, what's not working, our coaches know, and so we can call stuff that uh you know, we feel like it has a better chance. >> You gave him his debut. You went to him I think four times in the one drive and said four. >> Yeah, I mean, he created some separation, made some contested catches, and then made a rookie play, but uh I thought I saw some growth. I'm proud of him. He's a good kid, cares about it. Um we're going to need him to, you know, keep improving. >> And the two more guys in the game of telling Mike what's working, what's not working, how do you kind of assess the play calling today and just in the last 2 weeks with the bigger sample size? >> No, it's not that big of a sample size, but you know, I thought we didn't execute very well at all. The play plays were fine. Um we had opportunities, and we got to dig into the details on some of this stuff. If there's too much stuff in the plan, we got to cut it back. I'm always liking to push the envelope, and if I see you know, guys doing it the right way in practice, then I feel good about it. But we got to try and transfer the practice to the to the game, obviously, and the details got to come with it. >> Mike McCarthy has taken a lot of ownership, saying he needs to do better. Just what have you seen from him in these early moments of first adversity within the team? >> Yeah, I mean, I've seen Mike for 14 years, so Mike uh is going to take accountability. Sometimes when it's not his fault, doesn't need to do that, but um you know, Mike loves the guys, and he and he wants us to uh to have some urgency and to bounce back with this, and I I know we will. >> All right, thanks, guys. >> Okay. >> [sighs and snorts] >> We're not divided at all. Oh, yeah. I mean, anytime we we play this game to win. So, anytime you don't come out with a win, you are left trying to figure out what happened. >> What did What did you guys like about some of the plays you were able to create defensively and how you guys played for a couple of games? >> I feel like I mean, it's on the tape. We have a lot of great players. We have great scheme. I feel like we can create havoc in the backfield. It's just a matter of I think today was just the explosive. There was like three or four explosive plays that can't happen. They're devastating when you when you play good football around and let those three or four it sucks. >> Talking about how the best teams often play or lead. What's your message to some of the teammates? What do you try to do to lead from the front here? >> All I know is to go back to work. Win, loss, draw, you got to go back to work. >> What was the message from Mike McCarthy in the locker room? >> I'll keep that private. >> You mentioned the big plays like last week. I think the longest play was 26. They had like five over 30. How do those those explosive plays um obviously they hurt you? What what anything in particular that was happening with those explosive plays? >> I'll have to go back and look at it. Obviously, they're unacceptable. You can't have any explosives, especially when you're playing good football everywhere else. As a defense, I think in the NFL, man, if you bust a coverage, if you don't rush when you're supposed to rush or whatever. Those those things get exposed quickly. >> You've been around Aaron for a little while now. What have you seen from him in terms of how he's able to bounce back and and get to the next week? >> Uh he's even keel, man. He's seen a lot of football. Um it's it's still very early, but we definitely have a sense of urgency. >> PJ, I know you've been around Herb for a long time. He forced that fumble, kind of punched it out like you used to do all the time or still do. Um but can you just take me through his growth from edge rusher off-ball taking and all always doing his job? >> Yeah, I mean I hats off to Herb. Truly a a great locker room guy, a good teammate, a guy that's continually on the rise, a guy that will do whatever he has to do to help this team win. And I have a lot of respect for him and his mentality. And the football gods pay those guys off. Um he works hard um and he performs well on Sundays consistently. >> PJ, uh Aaron said that he's sent by that roller coaster. In your history, how do you ride that roller coaster when you're up one down? >> Go back to work. Like I like I said earlier, man. You just you got to work. This is a what have you done for me lately type of business. So, you just got to go back to work no matter what. >> Anything else? >> Thanks, guys. >> Thank you, guys.

Your team every day. >> Welcome inside today's episode of Locked On Commanders. I'm your host, your guy on the ground, David Harrison. But first, why Jaden Daniels long-term health has to outweigh the immediate urgency surrounding Washington football this season. The priority in Washington bottom line has got to be getting Jaden Daniels right for the long term. It can't just be getting Jaden Daniels back as quickly as possible because that is just a recipe to get right back into the same situation the Washington Commanders find themselves in after their week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. It's much bigger than 0 and2 is much bigger than 0 and2 in the division. So, let's start with we actually with what we actually know. Likely by the time you're listening to this, watching this episode, you already know Jaden Daniels suffered an elbow injury in the week 2 loss against the Dallas Cowboys. The same injury he injured against the Seattle Seahawks. same injury he aggravated against the Minnesota Vikings which was the last time we saw him play in 2025 and since that aggravation in Minnesota in 2025 we've seen him play exactly one full NFL game week one loss against Philadelphia Eagles and then half a game exactly right down to the tick of the zero second in the first half mark we got to see him play another half a game so one and a half games total since the last time he aggravated that elbow injury and he dislocated the elbow again it is a dislocation Dan Quinn shared The initial X-ray showed no fracture in the elbow. He was able to travel home with his team and his teammates on Sunday night. More imaging is coming, which is always the case. And Dan Quinn said that his expectation for Jaden Daniels returning is optimistic. He does believe that Jaden Daniels will probably be able to return this season, but that's not something that is supported by an actual prognosis or timeline, things like that as of right now. So, I think that kind of brings up the question of this has to be not how soon can Jaden get back on the field. It's got to be what gives Jaden Daniels the best chance to resume his journey or his development into the franchise quarterback for this organization that I think most people uh if not everybody believes that he absolutely can be and has shown the potential to be because dislocating your elbow while falling and bracing yourself under your own body weight is a fluke injury. The fact that it's happened now twice in the last four games that this this quarterback has played in the National Football League regular season, that's not a fluke. That is a pattern. That is a structural problem with Jaden Daniels non-throwing arm that needs to be figured out. It's it's got to get figured out. It's got to get solved or else Jaden is is at risk of going down as one of those players uh in the NFL who could have been great, should have been great, showed all the potential to be great and injuries on ultimately derailed his potential. We've seen it before this very franchise with RG3. We've seen it. We've seen it with other players as well. And nobody wants to see Jaden Daniels go down that path. Dan Quinn after the game said, quote, "Man, we are bummed for him. I thought he was really playing his ass off. We will rally so hard around Marcus Mariota until Jaden's back." End quote. And the second half of that quote is really what kind of stood out to me. Until Jaden's back, not until they can get him back. It's until he's back. And I think you have you got to do this the right way. You got to make sure that you're protecting the franchise's future, not just trying to do what's best for 2026. And we go back to Dan Quinn all the time says he likes to do the hard right instead of the easy wrong. That would be the hard right is doing this the right way. Get Jane Daniels back only when it's it's ready, only when the the elbow is ready, and only when there is a plan in place, whether that's procedural, whether that's braces, whether that's whatever it is to get that thing right and get that thing figured out. Now, the same elbow, the fact this is the same elbow is part of this absolute com conversation because it's not just a random ankle sprain. It's not just a random unrelated injury. It's a dislocation. The exact same elbow really in much the exact same way. It wasn't outside the pocket running away and all that kind of stuff, but it was much the same type of way. He was landing on that arm, doing all those things. My expectation which comes with no medical degree and no inside knowledge uh is is or no inside knowledge other than what Dan Quinn has told us is no earlier than week eight which is after the bye-week. So you got uh you got one more game Seattle Seahawks at home then you got the game in London then you come back for New York you on the road San Francisco by week after that then you come back week eight at home against the Philadelphia Eagles. I think that is the earliest and that is by far the left margin. Like that is that may even be a little bit too aggressive. And again, this is just kind of what I'm anticipating, not what I'm reporting. Of course, we'll continue to hear from Dan Quinn about those things. But when you look at this same injury last year and what the Washington Commanders did, it's it's roughly the same time frame as far as time missed and time not playing football. But we all kind of agreed, I think, that when he went back onto the field against the Minnesota Vikings, did have that brace on, said he didn't like it, all those things. Got knocked to the ground trying to cover an interception return and it just it didn't look right. He landed on it and immediately you just tell like he was not supposed to be out there and and I feel like they just kind of allowed anticipation of like, hey, we're still in the playoff hunt. We still want to do this. Jaden wants to do this. He's a warrior. All this kind of stuff. They let that get the better of him. And look, nobody's perfect. It's going to happen. and it's happened before, it'll happen again. But you got to learn from it, right? Tomorrow's imaging. Monday's imaging. I think, you know, if there's a revelation there of something that can be done long term as a solution, you've got to be able to sacrifice games without Jaden this season to get this thing done right so that you can potentially have him for like the next decade plus. And again, not a doctor here, but done some research, talked to people who are smarter about this stuff than I am. There is a procedure. I don't know what it's called. I don't know like the intricacies of it, but there is a procedure that be can be done to kind of the way it was said to me was tighten everything up inside that elbow because basically what it boils down to from my understanding is it's a ligament issue, not like a torn issue, but like a a ligament issue where the ligaments are not are not strong enough and when he lands on that arm basically when that elbow tries to pop out, those ligaments don't hold them hold that in. Again, that's like I think that's like the fifth grade version, right?
